A Calculus of Verified Behavior Inclusions for Agent-Authored Systems

Section titled “A Calculus of Verified Behavior Inclusions for Agent-Authored Systems”

Formal Technical Report · November 2026

Abstract

Section titled “Abstract”

Autonomous coding agents fail in three recurring ways. They leap from a requirement to code and invent the missing design; they lose the rationale for load-bearing choices and later weaken tests to make builds pass; and they leave humans with no trustworthy intermediate view of what the system does. This report presents a refinement-DAG calculus that structures software development as an acyclic graph of verified behavior inclusions. A development record assigns each cell its active intents, support provenance, contextual models, state machines, a decomposition into child contracts, and evidence. One relation — behavior inclusion under a typed edge abstraction map — serves for intent satisfaction, child contract refinement, connector decomposition, and code realization. The partial-order acyclicity of the Refinement DAG from root specifications to executable leaves turns support evaluation into an acyclic topological evaluation, sibling verification into a substitution lemma, inspection into elementary closure and cut subgraph extraction, and version evolution into proof reuse at unchanged interfaces. The central theorem states that a valid refinement DAG refines all admitted root intents, conditional on explicit executable-realization and profile-admissibility premises. The report develops the DAG definition, subgraph and cut extraction with frontier soundness, the refinement-DAG soundness proof, the cutoff theorem, a five-gate agent protocol, a four-step evolution loop, and a complete durable-acknowledgement example, and it relates the paper calculus to a checked Lean 4 mechanization kernel.

1. Introduction

Section titled “1. Introduction”

1.1 The problem

Section titled “1.1 The problem”

An agent is asked to add a feature or change a subsystem. It receives a requirement sentence and produces code. Between the sentence and the code lie decisions the sentence does not contain: data layout, ownership, error semantics, protocol ordering, retry policy, concurrency control, and edge-case handling. When the agent fills that gap in one leap, three failures follow.

Wide abstraction leap. The agent invents the missing design while writing the implementation. Implicit choices become hidden assumptions: a synchronous clock, a lossless channel, an atomic write that is not atomic, a lock that is not held across the operation that needs it. The resulting system can pass unit tests and still violate the requirement under interleaving, failure, or scale.

Rationale erasure and silent test weakening. A source repository records the final code, not the ordered argument for why a structure or protocol was chosen from upstream constraints, nor why the alternatives were rejected. A later agent cannot distinguish a load-bearing invariant from an incidental detail. Faced with a failing test, the cheapest repair is often to delete the assertion or weaken the condition. The build passes; the invariant is gone.

Human inscrutability. There is no trustworthy intermediate view. To know what the system does, a human must read thousands of lines of agent-generated code, reconstruct the design from the implementation, and guess which parts are intentional. Review degrades into rubber-stamping or line-by-line debugging.

1.2 Why post-hoc auditing does not address the problem

Section titled “1.2 Why post-hoc auditing does not address the problem”

An audit that runs after the code exists can detect some violations, but it does not prevent the leap that produced them. A diff algorithm can show what changed, but it cannot show which invariant the change was supposed to preserve. A test suite can encode a requirement, but a test is evidence about a sample, not a proof of a universal behavioral obligation, and it is exactly the artifact an agent can weaken. The problem is structural: the development process has no mandatory intermediate objects that are both behavioral and checkable.

1.3 The Refinement-DAG thesis

Section titled “1.3 The Refinement-DAG thesis”

Development proceeds through a finite Refinement DAG

G=(V, M, χ, I, J, E)G = \bigl(V,\ \mathcal{M},\ \chi,\ I,\ J,\ E\bigr)G=(V, M, χ, I, J, E)

rooted at top-level system requirements and terminating at executable leaves.

At each cell v∈Vv \in Vv∈V, the developer records:

  • the intents active at vvv and the acyclic upstream support links that activate them;
  • the context premises and design rationales for vvv, with alternatives and reopening conditions;
  • an explicit state machine MvM_vMv​ for vvv;
  • if vvv is an internal cell (ch⁡(v)≠∅\operatorname{ch}(v) \neq \emptysetch(v)=∅), a decomposition into child contracts for its direct successors ch⁡(v)\operatorname{ch}(v)ch(v); if vvv is a leaf (ch⁡(v)=∅\operatorname{ch}(v) = \emptysetch(v)=∅), an executable program PvP_vPv​;
  • evidence that the cell’s machine satisfies its intents and that its decomposition or realization is sound.

A candidate advances only when the required checks at that cell and its outgoing edges succeed. Leaf cells (Vleaf={ℓ∈V∣ch⁡(ℓ)=∅}V_{\mathrm{leaf}} = \{\ell \in V \mid \operatorname{ch}(\ell) = \emptyset\}Vleaf​={ℓ∈V∣ch(ℓ)=∅}) carry executable programs under declared execution semantics. Stringent development validity includes the operational realization of connector wiring and the selected profile’s initialization, input, and progress conditions; the soundness theorem is conditional on them. The result is a DAG of behavior inclusions, where every link is small enough to verify and every link is retained as evidence.

The prevention claim is precise. An implementation that violates a protected, formally expressed obligation cannot be accepted by a sound gate whose complete dependencies are preserved. The gate does not make the agent intelligent; it makes the agent’s obligations explicit, local, ordered, and checkable.

1.4 Contributions

Section titled “1.4 Contributions”
  1. A refinement calculus in which intent satisfaction, child contract refinement, connector decomposition, and code realization are one relation: behavior inclusion under a typed edge abstraction map.
  2. A partial-formalization spectrum that accommodates coarsened contracts (universal top, type/shape, pre/post, invariants) alongside full protocol machines, paired with an evidence discipline that bridges bounded/sampled test evidence and universal behavioral obligations without unprincipled claims.
  3. An acyclic topological support evaluation with a separate evidence stratum and a protected-obligation preservation rule, so neither a failed check nor a support edit silently erases the obligation.
  4. A Refinement-DAG soundness theorem whose chain is leaf realization, connector monotonicity, child refinement, and inclusion transitivity, established by well-founded induction on the DAG under explicit typing, shared-singleton scoping, and input-admissibility premises.
  5. Elementary subgraph and cross-section extraction on the DAG using three set primitives—predecessor closure, successor closure, and root-covering cuts—with pointwise and frontier soundness guarantees.
  6. A sibling-independence theorem with explicit composition conditions, including interaction ownership, executable closure, and practical integration recipes for third-party libraries and shared stateful services (databases, caches, queues).
  7. An incremental frame and interface cutoff theorem: a versioned evolution model where modifications, splits, merges, or refactorings reuse every unchanged obligation proposition by identity, providing semantic behavioral caching for CI/CD test-impact analysis and requiring zero ancestor solver re-execution.
  8. A five-gate development protocol and a four-step evolution loop, including a repair taxonomy that separates semantic counterexamples, failed proof witnesses, and unresolved checker results.
  9. A complete durable-acknowledgement example, worked through a two-level Refinement DAG with a single-use interface precondition, a visible durability observation, leaf pseudocode, an agent error, its counterexample, and two repair paths.
  10. A mechanization target whose algebraic and DAG-soundness kernel is checked in Lean 4.

1.5 Roadmap

Section titled “1.5 Roadmap”

Section 2 fixes the refinement algebra, typed edge abstractions, observation extension (including complexity bounds), admissible input restrictions, and the spectrum of contract precision. Section 3 defines the Refinement DAG, support evaluation, context premises, validity, the DAG soundness theorem, and subgraph/cut extraction with frontier soundness. Section 4 details the verification obligations, evidence discipline, and pragmatics for bounded/sampled evidence. Section 5 treats decomposition, connectors, sibling independence, and practical integration recipes for third-party libraries and shared infrastructure. Section 6 gives the development protocol. Section 7 gives versioned evolution, contextual intent projection, exact obligation propositions, the incremental frame theorem, CI/CD semantic caching, and the evolution loop. Section 8 works the durable-acknowledgement example. Section 9 specifies the mechanization target and relates it to JirlCalculus.lean. Sections 10–11 cover related work and open problems. Appendices A–B give expanded proof details and notation.

2. The Refinement Algebra

Section titled “2. The Refinement Algebra”

2.1 Observations, machines, and specifications

Section titled “2.1 Observations, machines, and specifications”

Fix an interface XXX. An observation space OX\mathcal{O}_XOX​ is a set of observations of XXX. The core instance is the set of finite traces over the visible actions of XXX; the liveness instance adds maximal traces under a declared fairness condition; the timed and probabilistic instances replace traces with timed or measure-valued observations. A specification at XXX is a subset Φ⊆OX\Phi \subseteq \mathcal{O}_XΦ⊆OX​.

A machine at XXX is a structure

M=(S,S0,Σ,→,obsM)M = (S, S_0, \Sigma, \to, \mathrm{obs}_M)M=(S,S0​,Σ,→,obsM​)

where SSS is a state set, S0⊆SS_0 \subseteq SS0​⊆S the initial states, Σ\SigmaΣ a partitioned alphabet of inputs, outputs, and internal actions, →⊆S×Σ×S\to \subseteq S \times \Sigma \times S→⊆S×Σ×S the transition relation, and obsM\mathrm{obs}_MobsM​ maps executions to observations. Its behavior is

beh⁡(M)={ obsM(ρ)∣ρ is an execution of M }⊆OX.\operatorname{beh}(M) = \{\, \mathrm{obs}_M(\rho) \mid \rho \text{ is an execution of } M \,\} \subseteq \mathcal{O}_X .beh(M)={obsM​(ρ)∣ρ is an execution of M}⊆OX​.

For the trace kernel, beh⁡(M)\operatorname{beh}(M)beh(M) is a trace set and is written tr⁡(M)\operatorname{tr}(M)tr(M).

Observation extension & emergent child properties (e.g., complexity bounds). The single inclusion relation ⊆\subseteq⊆ handles the case where a parent does not constrain complexity while a child introduces a high-performance complexity bound. When the child’s observation space OXc\mathcal{O}_{X_c}OXc​​ extends observations with resource or cost dimensions (τ,size,cost)(\tau, \mathrm{size}, \mathrm{cost})(τ,size,cost) that αv,c\alpha_{v,c}αv,c​ projects out to τ∈OXv,c\tau \in \mathcal{O}_{X_{v,c}}τ∈OXv,c​​, satisfying both the parent slot contract Bv,cB_{v,c}Bv,c​ and the child’s local complexity specification Φccost={o∈OXc∣cost⁡(o)≤f(size⁡(o))}\Phi_c^{\mathrm{cost}} = \{o \in \mathcal{O}_{X_c} \mid \operatorname{cost}(o) \le f(\operatorname{size}(o))\}Φccost​={o∈OXc​​∣cost(o)≤f(size(o))} is a single pullback-intersection inclusion:

Note that exporting a whole-parent complexity bound requires a cost-preserving observation space at vvv and a cost-composition law on KvK_vKv​.

General-purpose children & admissible input histories. Reusable child components (standard library modules, general database clients, utility data structures) typically accept a wider domain of inputs than any single parent uses. Let HXcin\mathcal{H}_{X_c}^{\mathrm{in}}HXc​in​ denote the space of input histories at child interface XcX_cXc​, and let πin:OXc→HXcin\pi_{\mathrm{in}} : \mathcal{O}_{X_c} \to \mathcal{H}_{X_c}^{\mathrm{in}}πin​:OXc​​→HXc​in​ project an observation to its input history prefix. When parent vvv‘s connector WvW_vWv​ guarantees that input histories supplied to child ccc lie within an admissible set Av,c⊆HXcinA_{v,c} \subseteq \mathcal{H}_{X_c}^{\mathrm{in}}Av,c​⊆HXc​in​, write beh⁡(Mc) ⁣↾Av,c\operatorname{beh}(M_c)\!\upharpoonright_{A_{v,c}}beh(Mc​)↾Av,c​​ for the restricted behavior set:

beh⁡(Mc) ⁣↾Av,c  =  { o∈beh⁡(Mc)  ∣  πin(o)∈Av,c }.\operatorname{beh}(M_c)\!\upharpoonright_{A_{v,c}} \;=\; \bigl\{\, o \in \operatorname{beh}(M_c) \;\big|\; \pi_{\mathrm{in}}(o) \in A_{v,c} \,\bigr\}.beh(Mc​)↾Av,c​​={o∈beh(Mc​)​πin​(o)∈Av,c​}.

The edge refinement obligation under admissible input restriction is:

αv,c(beh⁡(Mc) ⁣↾Av,c)  ⊆  beh⁡(Bv,c),\alpha_{v,c}\bigl(\operatorname{beh}(M_c)\!\upharpoonright_{A_{v,c}}\bigr) \;\subseteq\; \operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c}),αv,c​(beh(Mc​)↾Av,c​​)⊆beh(Bv,c​),

accompanied by input receptiveness and progress preservation on Av,cA_{v,c}Av,c​.

The Admissible-Input Delivery Premise. Restricted refinement does not imply global refinement: an implementation may behave arbitrarily outside Av,cA_{v,c}Av,c​. For restricted refinement to soundly substitute into parent composition, the parent connector KvK_vKv​ and concrete wiring CvC_vCv​ must satisfy the admissible-input delivery premise: every trajectory admitted by WvW_vWv​ projects onto child ccc with an input history in Av,cA_{v,c}Av,c​. Under this premise, Beh⁡(Cv[Qc])=Beh⁡(Cv[Qc ⁣↾Av,c])\operatorname{Beh}(C_v[Q_c]) = \operatorname{Beh}(C_v[Q_c\!\upharpoonright_{A_{v,c}}])Beh(Cv​[Qc​])=Beh(Cv​[Qc​↾Av,c​​]), ensuring that restricting the child’s behavioral domain introduces no unsoundness at the parent.

The Spectrum of Contract Precision (Coarsened Contracts). In real-world software engineering, teams cannot and should not write complete, cycle-accurate state machine models for every commodity helper or standard library call on Day 1. The partial-order inclusion relation ⊆\subseteq⊆ natively supports a continuous spectrum of contract precision without breaking the mathematical integrity of the DAG:

  1. Level 0 — Unconstrained Top Contract (⊤\top⊤). At the coarsest extreme, an unconstrained contract Bv,c=OXv,cB_{v,c} = \mathcal{O}_{X_{v,c}}Bv,c​=OXv,c​​ admits all possible observations. Any implementation trivially satisfies beh⁡(Mc)⊆⊤\operatorname{beh}(M_c) \subseteq \topbeh(Mc​)⊆⊤. This allows teams to introduce placeholder cells during initial architectural scaffolding without inventing fictitious formalisms.
  2. Level 1 — Type and Shape Contracts. Over a value- or schema-observation projection αv,c\alpha_{v,c}αv,c​, an interface contract Bv,cB_{v,c}Bv,c​ constrains value types, data shapes, or memory safety. Under the language’s type-soundness theorem, the projected inclusion αv,c(beh⁡(Mc))⊆beh⁡(Bv,c)\alpha_{v,c}(\operatorname{beh}(M_c)) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c})αv,c​(beh(Mc​))⊆beh(Bv,c​) for that type/shape slice is discharged statically by the compiler type checker (e.g., Rust, TypeScript, Lean 4) without dynamic state-space exploration.
  3. Level 2 — Pre/Post Functional Contracts (Hoare Style). Over an input-output observation projection, Bv,c={(in,out)∣P(in)  ⟹  Q(in,out)}B_{v,c} = \{(\mathrm{in}, \mathrm{out}) \mid P(\mathrm{in}) \implies Q(\mathrm{in}, \mathrm{out})\}Bv,c​={(in,out)∣P(in)⟹Q(in,out)} leaves behavior outside precondition PPP unconstrained (⊤\top⊤). Under Hoare-logic soundness, this projected inclusion is discharged via deductive verifiers, SMT solvers, or exhaustive bounded checkers (e.g., Dafny, Creusot).
  4. Level 3 — Stateful Protocol Machines & Invariants. For concurrency-critical, durable, or safety-critical components (e.g., consensus, WAL, authentication protocols), Bv,cB_{v,c}Bv,c​ specifies an explicit transition system with temporal safety invariants, visible event orderings, and liveness duties. Discharged via inductive simulation witnesses or certified model checkers.

Because every level is an instance of behavior set inclusion ⊆\subseteq⊆, a Refinement DAG can freely combine coarsened contracts on commodity glue code with high-precision protocol machines on the critical spine. A subsystem can be progressively strengthened from Level 1 to Level 3 over time without modifying its ancestors, governed by Theorem 3.

2.3 Connectors

Section titled “2.3 Connectors”

A connector at a parent cell vvv is a map on behavior sets Kv:∏c∈ch⁡(v)P(OXv,c)⟶P(OXv)K_v : \prod_{c \in \operatorname{ch}(v)} \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{O}_{X_{v,c}}) \longrightarrow \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{O}_{X_v})Kv​:∏c∈ch(v)​P(OXv,c​​)⟶P(OXv​​), and it is admissible when it is monotone:

Bv,c⊆Bv,c′ for all c∈ch⁡(v)  ⟹  Kv({Bv,c}c)⊆Kv({Bv,c′}c).B_{v,c} \subseteq B'_{v,c} \text{ for all } c \in \operatorname{ch}(v) \;\Longrightarrow\; K_v(\{B_{v,c}\}_c) \subseteq K_v(\{B'_{v,c}\}_c).Bv,c​⊆Bv,c′​ for all c∈ch(v)⟹Kv​({Bv,c​}c​)⊆Kv​({Bv,c′​}c​).

The operational reading is a wiring skeleton WvW_vWv​ that routes, synchronizes, interleaves, and hides child actions, with no state of its own that is not visible in the children or in a declared substrate primitive. A trajectory model of WvW_vWv​ supplies:

  • a set legal⁡Wv\operatorname{legal}_{W_v}legalWv​​ of legal shared trajectories rrr;
  • for each child ccc, a slice slice⁡c(r)\operatorname{slice}_c(r)slicec​(r) in OXv,c\mathcal{O}_{X_{v,c}}OXv,c​​;
  • a projection obs⁡v(r)\operatorname{obs}_v(r)obsv​(r) in OXv\mathcal{O}_{X_v}OXv​​.

The induced transformer is

Kv({Bv,c}c)={ obs⁡v(r)  ∣  legal⁡Wv(r) ∧ ∀c∈ch⁡(v). slice⁡c(r)∈Bv,c }.K_v(\{B_{v,c}\}_c) = \bigl\{\, \operatorname{obs}_v(r) \;\big|\; \operatorname{legal}_{W_v}(r) \ \wedge\ \forall c \in \operatorname{ch}(v).\ \operatorname{slice}_c(r) \in B_{v,c} \,\bigr\}.Kv​({Bv,c​}c​)={obsv​(r)​legalWv​​(r) ∧ ∀c∈ch(v). slicec​(r)∈Bv,c​}.

Lemma 1 (Trajectory connectors are monotone). If Bv,c⊆Bv,c′B_{v,c} \subseteq B'_{v,c}Bv,c​⊆Bv,c′​ for every c∈ch⁡(v)c \in \operatorname{ch}(v)c∈ch(v), then Kv({Bv,c}c)⊆Kv({Bv,c′}c)K_v(\{B_{v,c}\}_c) \subseteq K_v(\{B'_{v,c}\}_c)Kv​({Bv,c​}c​)⊆Kv​({Bv,c′​}c​).

Proof. Take o∈Kv({Bv,c}c)o \in K_v(\{B_{v,c}\}_c)o∈Kv​({Bv,c​}c​). There is a legal rrr with obs⁡v(r)=o\operatorname{obs}_v(r) = oobsv​(r)=o and slice⁡c(r)∈Bv,c\operatorname{slice}_c(r) \in B_{v,c}slicec​(r)∈Bv,c​ for every ccc. Since Bv,c⊆Bv,c′B_{v,c} \subseteq B'_{v,c}Bv,c​⊆Bv,c′​, each slice lies in Bv,c′B'_{v,c}Bv,c′​ as well, so o∈Kv({Bv,c′}c)o \in K_v(\{B'_{v,c}\}_c)o∈Kv​({Bv,c′​}c​). ■\blacksquare■

The trajectory model is the mathematical content of the wiring. Its operational soundness obligation is that the implementation of WvW_vWv​ produces only observations in the transformer’s output. This is where routing, synchronization, initialization, and shared-resource behavior are established. It is a property of the connector, discharged once per wiring pattern, not a per-child obligation.

The algebra is small on purpose. The paper’s correctness argument is the transitive closure of this table, and the engineering content is the discipline that decides what to put on each side.

2.5 Semantic profiles

Section titled “2.5 Semantic profiles”

A semantic profile Γ\GammaΓ fixes the observation class and the obligations that accompany it:

  • Safety profile. Observations are finite visible traces; M⪯AM \preceq AM⪯A is trace inclusion.
  • Liveness profile. Observations are maximal traces under a declared fairness condition; refinement preserves maximality and fairness, and a progress obligation accompanies the trace inclusion.
  • Timed and probabilistic profiles. Observations are timed traces or path measures; refinement uses the corresponding measurable or timed preorder.

Two side conditions belong to every open-interface profile:

  • Input receptiveness. If a contract permits an input at a related state, the child must accept it. Without this condition, a child can satisfy a safety contract by refusing every request, which is not an admissible replacement.
  • Progress preservation. For a liveness contract, the child must preserve the required maximal fair executions. Finite-prefix inclusion alone admits a machine that accepts a request and then stops.

The core theorems are stated for the trace profile with these two side conditions. The timed and probabilistic instantiations use the same graph structure and the same schema; only the profile’s refinement relation and composition lemma change.

2.6 Boundary discipline

Section titled “2.6 Boundary discipline”

A contract constrains observable behavior at the child interface and the child’s duties to the connector. It may specify:

  • the inputs the child must accept;
  • the outputs it may produce and their order;
  • relations between its outputs and shared connector state;
  • progress or termination duties;
  • the environment assumptions under which those duties hold.

It does not prescribe the child’s internal algorithm, data layout, module structure, or implementation strategy. The child is free to choose any implementation whose behavior lies within the contract. This is the boundary rule that makes independent development possible: the parent owns the interface; the child owns the implementation.

3.2 Active intents and topological support evaluation

Section titled “3.2 Active intents and topological support evaluation”

The active intents A⊆IA \subseteq IA⊆I are defined as the least fixed point:

c∈A  ⟺  c∈Iroot  ∨  ∃P∈J(c). P⊆A.c \in A \iff c \in I^{\mathrm{root}} \;\lor\; \exists P \in J(c).\ P \subseteq A.c∈A⟺c∈Iroot∨∃P∈J(c). P⊆A.

Because the support relation JJJ is acyclic on the finite set III, AAA is evaluated deterministically in a single forward pass along any topological order of (I,J)(I, J)(I,J) without circularity.

Lemma 2 (Evidence separation). AAA is a function of (I,J)(I, J)(I,J) only and does not mention EEE. Consequently, a failed, missing, or pending evidence record leaves every obligation it concerns active and blocking.

Proof. The fixed-point condition defining AAA refers only to intent records and support links. The evidence stratum EEE does not occur in it. ■\blacksquare■

3.3 Context premises, design provenance, and staleness

Section titled “3.3 Context premises, design provenance, and staleness”

Architectural choices—including contract declaration, connector selection, and component decomposition—are recorded at cell boundaries. For each cell v∈Vv \in Vv∈V, its local context premises ΔPv\Delta P_vΔPv​ form a finite set of references to upstream intents, parent contracts, and environmental assumptions on which vvv‘s model and decomposition depend, with transitive upstream closure ΔPv∗\Delta P_v^*ΔPv∗​. Superseded or alternative design options are preserved as historical snapshots in the version sequence {Gt}t∈N\{G_t\}_{t \in \mathbb{N}}{Gt​}t∈N​.

If an upstream intent or context premise xxx changes, downstream components in its dependency closure become stale:

stale⁡(x)={ v∈V∣x∈ΔPv∗ }.\operatorname{stale}(x) = \{\, v \in V \mid x \in \Delta P_v^* \,\}.stale(x)={v∈V∣x∈ΔPv∗​}.

Because prerequisites are strictly upstream, the reference graph is acyclic and the stale set is computed in linear time. A stale premise blocks publication of every cell that depends on it until re-warranted or replaced.

A development DAG G=(V,M,χ,I,J,E)G = (V, \mathcal{M}, \chi, I, J, E)G=(V,M,χ,I,J,E) is valid when conditions 1–6 hold for GGG (and condition 7 holds when publishing GGG as a versioned update to an existing development):

The operational instance Beh⁡exec(v)⊆Kv({αv,c(Beh⁡exec(c))}c)\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(v) \subseteq K_v(\{\alpha_{v,c}(\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(c))\}_c)Behexec​(v)⊆Kv​({αv,c​(Behexec​(c))}c​) follows by application to executable child behaviors (whose underlying execution witnesses are admissible by condition 6). For a leaf ℓ∈Vleaf\ell \in V_{\mathrm{leaf}}ℓ∈Vleaf​, evidence EEE certifies Beh⁡exec(ℓ)=beh⁡(Pℓ)⊆beh⁡(Mℓ)\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(\ell) = \operatorname{beh}(P_\ell) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_\ell)Behexec​(ℓ)=beh(Pℓ​)⊆beh(Mℓ​), with a nonempty initial state set.
  6. Profile admissibility. The selected semantic profile’s conditions hold:
    • Initialization. Initial states are within the invariant, and initial state sets are nonempty.
    • Input receptiveness. If a contract permits an input at a related state, the child accepts it.
    • Progress preservation. For liveness claims, required maximal fair executions are preserved.
  7. Protected obligation preservation. Every protected obligation active in the previous version remains active with identical semantic content and authority tag (preventing authority downgrades), unless an authorized disposition records its retirement, weakening, or re-classification (§3.8).

Conditions 1–6 define the intra-DAG validity of a development record GGG, and are the hypotheses consumed by the soundness theorem (Theorem 1). Condition 7 is the inter-version preservation condition consumed by the publication gate to prevent silent obligation erasure.

3.5 Edge refinement and the shared-child discipline

Section titled “3.5 Edge refinement and the shared-child discipline”

For every decomposition edge (v,c)(v,c)(v,c) with c∈ch⁡(v)c \in \operatorname{ch}(v)c∈ch(v), evidence EEE contains a valid record for edge refinement:

αv,c(beh⁡(Mc))⊆beh⁡(Bv,c)⟺beh⁡(Mc)⊆αv,c∗(beh⁡(Bv,c)).\alpha_{v,c}\bigl(\operatorname{beh}(M_c)\bigr) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c}) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{beh}(M_c) \subseteq \alpha_{v,c}^*\bigl(\operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c})\bigr).αv,c​(beh(Mc​))⊆beh(Bv,c​)⟺beh(Mc​)⊆αv,c∗​(beh(Bv,c​)).

When child refinement is restricted to admissible input histories Av,cA_{v,c}Av,c​ (§2.2), the edge obligation is αv,c(beh⁡(Mc) ⁣↾Av,c)⊆beh⁡(Bv,c)\alpha_{v,c}(\operatorname{beh}(M_c)\!\upharpoonright_{A_{v,c}}) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c})αv,c​(beh(Mc​)↾Av,c​​)⊆beh(Bv,c​) (with Av,c=HXcinA_{v,c} = \mathcal{H}_{X_c}^{\mathrm{in}}Av,c​=HXc​in​ for unrestricted edges). The edge refinement compares a child implementation with the contract its parent declared, under the edge abstraction map αv,c\alpha_{v,c}αv,c​. It does not compare the child with an obsolete implementation; the contract is the complete interface.

When a child cell ccc has multiple parents par⁡(c)={u1,…,um}\operatorname{par}(c) = \{u_1, \dots, u_m\}par(c)={u1​,…,um​} (a shared child in the DAG), two disciplines govern the shared node:

  1. Edge-indexed refinement. The child machine McM_cMc​ must simultaneously satisfy each incoming slot contract under that edge’s admissible input history set Au,cA_{u,c}Au,c​: ∀u∈par⁡(c),αu,c(beh⁡(Mc) ⁣↾Au,c)⊆beh⁡(Bu,c)⟺∀u∈par⁡(c),beh⁡(Mc) ⁣↾Au,c⊆αu,c∗(beh⁡(Bu,c)).\forall u \in \operatorname{par}(c),\quad \alpha_{u,c}\bigl(\operatorname{beh}(M_c)\!\upharpoonright_{A_{u,c}}\bigr) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(B_{u,c}) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \forall u \in \operatorname{par}(c),\quad \operatorname{beh}(M_c)\!\upharpoonright_{A_{u,c}} \subseteq \alpha_{u,c}^*\bigl(\operatorname{beh}(B_{u,c})\bigr).∀u∈par(c),αu,c​(beh(Mc​)↾Au,c​​)⊆beh(Bu,c​)⟺∀u∈par(c),beh(Mc​)↾Au,c​​⊆αu,c∗​(beh(Bu,c​)).
  2. Instance vs. singleton scope. If each parent instantiates a separate runtime copy of ccc (or ccc is purely stateless), edge-indexed refinement suffices. If parents share a single stateful runtime instance of ccc, Beh⁡exec(c)\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(c)Behexec​(c) and McM_cMc​ must range over the aggregate multi-client history owned at a selected common dominating ancestor boundary. The two-sentence shared-counter witness illustrates why: two clients that each expect 1 on their first call in isolation observe 1 and 2 when sharing one counter instance. Thus, separate isolated single-client contracts do not compose without accounting for multi-client interleavings at the dominating ancestor.

3.6 Refinement-DAG soundness

Section titled “3.6 Refinement-DAG soundness”

Theorem 1 (Refinement-DAG soundness). Let G=(V,M,χ,I,J,E)G = (V, \mathcal{M}, \chi, I, J, E)G=(V,M,χ,I,J,E) be a Refinement DAG. Suppose:

  • (A1) GGG satisfies the validity conditions 1–6 of §3.4;
  • (A2) every decomposition edge (v,c)(v,c)(v,c) with c∈ch⁡(v)c \in \operatorname{ch}(v)c∈ch(v) satisfies edge refinement αv,c(beh⁡(Mc) ⁣↾Av,c)⊆beh⁡(Bv,c)\alpha_{v,c}(\operatorname{beh}(M_c)\!\upharpoonright_{A_{v,c}}) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c})αv,c​(beh(Mc​)↾Av,c​​)⊆beh(Bv,c​) (§3.5), with Av,c=HXcinA_{v,c} = \mathcal{H}_{X_c}^{\mathrm{in}}Av,c​=HXc​in​ for unrestricted edges;
  • (A3) Typed edge abstraction compatibility: for each decomposition edge (v,c)(v,c)(v,c), abstraction map αv,c:OXc→OXv,c\alpha_{v,c} : \mathcal{O}_{X_c} \to \mathcal{O}_{X_{v,c}}αv,c​:OXc​​→OXv,c​​ maps child observations into the slot observation domain OXv,c\mathcal{O}_{X_{v,c}}OXv,c​​ consumed by connector KvK_vKv​ and contract Bv,cB_{v,c}Bv,c​;
  • (A4) Shared-singleton and input-admissibility scope: any shared stateful child cell ccc is scoped over aggregate multi-client histories at a selected common dominating ancestor boundary (§3.5, §5.4); and for any edge (v,c)(v,c)(v,c) using admissible-input restricted refinement (§2.2), parent wiring CvC_vCv​ and transformer KvK_vKv​ satisfy the admissible-input delivery premise.

Then for every cell v∈Vv \in Vv∈V, Beh⁡exec(v)⊆beh⁡(Mv)\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(v) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_v)Behexec​(v)⊆beh(Mv​), and for every active intent c∈A(v)c \in A(v)c∈A(v), Beh⁡exec(v)⊆⟦c⟧\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(v) \subseteq \llbracket c \rrbracketBehexec​(v)⊆[[c]]. In particular, for every root r∈Vrootr \in V_{\mathrm{root}}r∈Vroot​,

Beh⁡exec(r)⊆Φ(r)=⋂c∈A(r)⟦c⟧,\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(r) \subseteq \Phi(r) = \bigcap_{c \in A(r)} \llbracket c \rrbracket,Behexec​(r)⊆Φ(r)=c∈A(r)⋂​[[c]],

the semantic conjunction at root rrr, not the syntactic set A(r)A(r)A(r).

Proof. By well-founded induction on the finite acyclic child relation v→cv \to cv→c on VVV.

Base case (ℓ∈Vleaf\ell \in V_{\mathrm{leaf}}ℓ∈Vleaf​, ch⁡(ℓ)=∅\operatorname{ch}(\ell) = \emptysetch(ℓ)=∅). The proof is the spine of the calculus. It uses executable realization, monotonicity, child refinement, decomposition, and transitivity. Acyclicity enters in the well-founded induction: every child’s proof is a separate premise, and the parent’s decomposition is checked against contracts rather than against the concrete product of child states. The operational counterexample — identity KKK, child {ok}\{ok\}{ok}, parent {ok}\{ok\}{ok}, actual wiring {bad}\{bad\}{bad} — is excluded by condition 5, because {bad}⊆{ok}\{bad\} \subseteq \{ok\}{bad}⊆{ok} is false. The empty-initial-state counterexample is excluded by condition 6.

3.7 Subgraph extraction, cuts, and frontier soundness

Section titled “3.7 Subgraph extraction, cuts, and frontier soundness”

Human inspection and agent context scoping are formalized as information extraction on the finite DAG (V,ch⁡)(V, \operatorname{ch})(V,ch) using only three elementary set primitives and their intersections:

  1. Predecessor (Ancestor) Closure. Anc⁡(S)={ u∈V  ∣  ∃x∈S, u→∗x }.\operatorname{Anc}(S) = \{\, u \in V \;\mid\; \exists x \in S,\ u \to^* x \,\}.Anc(S)={u∈V∣∃x∈S, u→∗x}. This extracts the upstream provenance cone, answering why SSS exists and what requirements govern it.

  3. Root-Covering Cut (Frontier). An antichain C⊆VC \subseteq VC⊆V that intersects every directed path from VrootV_{\mathrm{root}}Vroot​ to VleafV_{\mathrm{leaf}}Vleaf​. Given a chosen focus antichain K⊆VK \subseteq VK⊆V contained in a root-covering cut C⊇KC \supseteq KC⊇K, the cut CCC extracts a complete horizontal cross-section passing through KKK.

Composite inspection views follow directly:

  • Connecting Interval between uuu and www: [u,w]=Desc⁡({u})∩Anc⁡({w})[u, w] = \operatorname{Desc}(\{u\}) \cap \operatorname{Anc}(\{w\})[u,w]=Desc({u})∩Anc({w});

Because architectural DAGs have modest size, all closure and cut extractions are evaluated directly by their set definitions without asymptotic complexity machinery.

The inspection direction is: every executable behavior maps under the abstractions to a behavior permitted by the cut’s machines, and every universal obligation displayed at cut CCC transfers to the code. The converse does not hold: an abstract cut model may admit behaviors that a concrete realization narrows. The cut view is an abstraction, not an equivalence.

3.8 Protected obligation preservation

Section titled “3.8 Protected obligation preservation”

Define the effective protected inventory of a version GGG:

Prot⁡(G)={(id⁡(c), ⟦c⟧, owner⁡(c), authority⁡(c))  ∣  c is active in G and authority⁡(c)∈{root,protected}}.\operatorname{Prot}(G) = \bigl\{(\operatorname{id}(c),\ \llbracket c \rrbracket,\ \operatorname{owner}(c),\ \operatorname{authority}(c)) \;\big|\; c \text{ is active in } G \text{ and } \operatorname{authority}(c) \in \{\mathrm{root}, \mathrm{protected}\}\bigr\}.Prot(G)={(id(c), [[c]], owner(c), authority(c))​c is active in G and authority(c)∈{root,protected}}.

A candidate G′G'G′ preserves GGG when for every p=(id⁡(c),⟦c⟧,owner⁡(c),auth)∈Prot⁡(G)p = (\operatorname{id}(c), \llbracket c \rrbracket, \operatorname{owner}(c), \mathrm{auth}) \in \operatorname{Prot}(G)p=(id(c),[[c]],owner(c),auth)∈Prot(G), either ppp is active in G′G'G′ with identical semantic content and unchanged authority tag (authority⁡G′(c)=auth\operatorname{authority}_{G'}(c) = \mathrm{auth}authorityG′​(c)=auth), or an authorized disposition d∈AG′d \in \mathcal{A}_{G'}d∈AG′​ (§7.1) records ppp, the authorization, and the rationale. A support edit, ownership change, interpretation change, or authority downgrade without such a disposition is rejected by validity condition 7. Ownership is total, so Prot⁡(G)\operatorname{Prot}(G)Prot(G) and the per-cell satisfaction sets range over the same active obligations; a protected interaction intent is assigned to the cell that owns the interaction boundary and is checked there.

Evidence failure does not deactivate an intent (Lemma 2), and any support, ownership, or authority edit that deactivates or downgrades a protected intent without a disposition is rejected by condition 7. Delegated intents may be refined or strengthened by agents, with any retirement recorded in the version provenance.

4. Verification Obligations

Section titled “4. Verification Obligations”

4.1 Satisfaction

Section titled “4.1 Satisfaction”

For a finite machine MvM_vMv​ and a specification Φ\PhiΦ, satisfaction is checked by exhaustive state-space exploration or by a certified invariant. For an infinite machine, it is checked by a theorem, a certified abstraction, or a bounded argument whose scope is recorded. The obligation is exactly beh⁡(Mv)⊆Φ(v)\operatorname{beh}(M_v) \subseteq \Phi(v)beh(Mv​)⊆Φ(v). A test is not, by itself, evidence for this universal inclusion. It is evidence for a bounded claim: no violation in the tested sample, or no violation within a bound. The evidence record must state the claim; the gate checks that the claim covers the obligation. A universal obligation is not discharged by a sampled test. A bounded intent can be discharged by a bounded check, provided the intent is stated with the same bound.

4.2 Decomposition and connector admissibility

Section titled “4.2 Decomposition and connector admissibility”

The decomposition obligation is

Kv({beh⁡(Bv,c)}c∈ch⁡(v))⊆beh⁡(Mv).K_v\bigl(\{\operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c})\}_{c \in \operatorname{ch}(v)}\bigr) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_v).Kv​({beh(Bv,c​)}c∈ch(v)​)⊆beh(Mv​).

It is checked at the parent cell against abstract child contracts, not against concrete child implementations. The connector’s admissibility relies on monotonicity (Lemma 1) and the universal wiring-adequacy certificate defined in §3.4 (condition 5), together with the interaction-ownership and reduction-preservation disciplines detailed in §5.6. A connector that fails these conditions lies outside the calculus until an explicit coordinator or reduction proof is supplied.

4.3 Child refinement

Section titled “4.3 Child refinement”

A child refinement obligation along decomposition edge (v,c)(v,c)(v,c) is

αv,c(beh⁡(Mc))⊆beh⁡(Bv,c)⟺beh⁡(Mc)⊆αv,c∗(beh⁡(Bv,c)).\alpha_{v,c}\bigl(\operatorname{beh}(M_c)\bigr) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c}) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \operatorname{beh}(M_c) \subseteq \alpha_{v,c}^*\bigl(\operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c})\bigr).αv,c​(beh(Mc​))⊆beh(Bv,c​)⟺beh(Mc​)⊆αv,c∗​(beh(Bv,c​)).

When child McM_cMc​ introduces local performance constraints or complexity bounds Φccost\Phi_c^{\mathrm{cost}}Φccost​, the single relation handles it as a pullback-intersection inclusion:

beh⁡(Mc)  ⊆  αv,c∗(beh⁡(Bv,c))  ∩  Φccost.\operatorname{beh}(M_c) \;\subseteq\; \alpha_{v,c}^*\bigl(\operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c})\bigr) \;\cap\; \Phi_c^{\mathrm{cost}}.beh(Mc​)⊆αv,c∗​(beh(Bv,c​))∩Φccost​.

When child McM_cMc​ is a general-purpose component whose full input domain exceeds what parent vvv‘s connector delivers, the edge obligation restricts to admissible input histories Av,cA_{v,c}Av,c​:

αv,c(beh⁡(Mc) ⁣↾Av,c)  ⊆  beh⁡(Bv,c),\alpha_{v,c}\bigl(\operatorname{beh}(M_c)\!\upharpoonright_{A_{v,c}}\bigr) \;\subseteq\; \operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c}),αv,c​(beh(Mc​)↾Av,c​​)⊆beh(Bv,c​),

accompanied by input receptiveness and progress preservation on Av,cA_{v,c}Av,c​.

For finite trace inclusion, an inductive simulation witness establishes it:

  • an invariant Ic⊆SMcI_c \subseteq S_{M_c}Ic​⊆SMc​​;
  • a relation Rc⊆SMc×SBv,cR_c \subseteq S_{M_c} \times S_{B_{v,c}}Rc​⊆SMc​​×SBv,c​​;
  • an action abstraction map λv,c\lambda_{v,c}λv,c​ from child actions to contract actions or silent steps.

The conditions are:

  1. Initiation. Every initial child state is in IcI_cIc​ and is related to an initial contract state.
  2. Consecution. IcI_cIc​ is closed under the child’s transitions.
  3. Step simulation. For (s,t)∈Rc(s, t) \in R_c(s,t)∈Rc​ and s→σs′s \xrightarrow{\sigma} s'sσ​s′: if λv,c(σ)=ϵ\lambda_{v,c}(\sigma) = \epsilonλv,c​(σ)=ϵ, then (s′,t)∈Rc(s', t) \in R_c(s′,t)∈Rc​; otherwise there is t′t't′ with t→λv,c(σ)t′t \xrightarrow{\lambda_{v,c}(\sigma)} t'tλv,c​(σ)​t′ and (s′,t′)∈Rc(s', t') \in R_c(s′,t′)∈Rc​.
  4. Input receptiveness. Every contract input enabled at ttt is enabled by some child input in λv,c−1\lambda_{v,c}^{-1}λv,c−1​ at sss.
  5. Silent convergence. For a liveness profile, a well-founded rank strictly decreases on silent steps, preventing infinite internal stuttering.

Lemma 3 (Finite-trace simulation). Conditions 1–3 imply λv,c(tr⁡(Mc))⊆tr⁡(Bv,c)\lambda_{v,c}(\operatorname{tr}(M_c)) \subseteq \operatorname{tr}(B_{v,c})λv,c​(tr(Mc​))⊆tr(Bv,c​).

Proof. Induct on the length of a child execution. Initiation relates the initial states. Consecution keeps the invariant. A silent step keeps the contract state; a visible step appends the matched contract transition. Every finite prefix therefore has a matching contract execution. ■\blacksquare■

For state-labeled properties, related states agree on the abstract valuations and silent steps preserve them. For liveness, the witness additionally preserves maximality and fairness, and validity condition 6 supplies the progress rank. For open inputs, simulation condition 4 blocks the trivial refusal strategy.

4.4 Realization

Section titled “4.4 Realization”

For each leaf cell ℓ∈Vleaf\ell \in V_{\mathrm{leaf}}ℓ∈Vleaf​, realization is certified by beh⁡(Pℓ)⊆beh⁡(Mℓ)\operatorname{beh}(P_\ell) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_\ell)beh(Pℓ​)⊆beh(Mℓ​) under the declared runtime semantics and environment assumptions. The substrate contract names what the runtime guarantees: an atomic write, a durable flush completion, or message delivery. For a decomposed parent cell, realization is discharged by the universal wiring-adequacy certificate (§3.4, condition 5), whose universal quantification over admissible child behaviors yields Beh⁡exec(v)⊆Kv({αv,c(Beh⁡exec(c))}c)\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(v) \subseteq K_v(\{\alpha_{v,c}(\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(c))\}_c)Behexec​(v)⊆Kv​({αv,c​(Behexec​(c))}c​) by application. For a leaf, it is the program-to-machine inclusion above.

4.5 Evidence discipline

Section titled “4.5 Evidence discipline”

An evidence record for an obligation ooo is a tuple

e=(o, method, claim, result, scope, artifact).e = (o,\ \mathrm{method},\ \mathrm{claim},\ \mathrm{result},\ \mathrm{scope},\ \mathrm{artifact}).e=(o, method, claim, result, scope, artifact).

It is valid for ooo when:

  1. claim\mathrm{claim}claim is at least as strong as ooo;
  2. method\mathrm{method}method is sound for claim\mathrm{claim}claim under scope\mathrm{scope}scope;
  3. result\mathrm{result}result is pass.

The result field is one of {pass,fail,unresolved,pending}\{\mathrm{pass}, \mathrm{fail}, \mathrm{unresolved}, \mathrm{pending}\}{pass,fail,unresolved,pending}. Only pass discharges an obligation; unresolved and pending are not passes and cannot enter the Verified outcome.

The method determines the claim:

Method Claim it can establish What it cannot establish
Proof derivation the exact obligation nothing beyond the logic’s soundness
Exhaustive finite model check the obligation for the modeled machine adequacy of the model to the code
Bounded model check the obligation up to the bound the unbounded obligation
Property-based test no violation in the sampled domain a universal inclusion
Runtime monitor no violation in the observed run future or unobserved behavior
Translation validation the specific program-to-machine relation unrelated properties

The scope records the observation profile, machine class, environment assumptions, and any bound. A result is meaningful only within its scope.

Evidence Pragmatics: Bridging Bounded/Sampled Evidence and Universal Obligations. In production software engineering, testing (unit, property-based, fuzzing, integration) represents the vast majority of day-to-day verification. JIRL reconciles real-world testing with mathematical rigor through three principled mechanisms:

  1. Scoped Bounded Intents. When universal verification is infeasible or unnecessary for a peripheral helper, the intent itself is stated with an explicit bound Φ≤k\Phi^{\le k}Φ≤k (e.g., “no unhandled exceptions within k=1000k=1000k=1000 event loops”, “schema conformance for payloads ≤64 KB\le 64\text{ KB}≤64 KB”). Bounded model checking or exhaustive bounded testing discharges this bounded obligation soundly with pass, without pretending to have proved an unbounded claim.
  2. Context Premise Domain Reduction (ΔPv\Delta P_vΔPv​). Teams can record explicit domain axioms or small-scope hypotheses in local context premises ΔPv\Delta P_vΔPv​ (e.g., “input strings are ASCII of length ≤8\le 8≤8”, “message queues with bounded capacity ≤4\le 4≤4”). When the declared premise restricts the relevant state and observation domain to a finite set, an exhaustive finite check over that finite state/observation domain discharges the universal claim under that explicit scope with pass. When the reachable state or observation domain remains infinite or check coverage is sampled, testing acts as a falsification probe and remains categorized as unresolved against universal claims. The premise is retained in the provenance ledger; if production telemetry reveals inputs violating ΔPv\Delta P_vΔPv​, the premise is marked stale, triggering reopening (§7.7).
  3. Provisional Development vs. Verified Publication. A property-based test (e.g., QuickCheck, Hypothesis) or sampled CI test suite evaluating a universal obligation serves as a valuable falsification probe. Its evidence record is stored with result=unresolved\mathrm{result} = \mathrm{unresolved}result=unresolved (or provisional test pass). The cell remains a development candidate: the gate G3 refuses to certify universal completion, preventing agents from claiming a full mathematical guarantee while giving human reviewers exact visibility into what has been tested versus what has been formally proved.

4.6 Evidence separation and the three-gate structure

Section titled “4.6 Evidence separation and the three-gate structure”

Every development has three independent gates:

  • Provenance gate. Every context premise ΔPv\Delta P_vΔPv​ is valid, its upstream dependencies hold, and no load-bearing premise is stale.
  • Behavioral gate. Every active intent has valid satisfaction evidence; every decomposition has valid evidence; every decomposition edge has valid child refinement evidence; every executable cell has valid realization evidence (wiring adequacy for a non-leaf cell, program-to-machine for a leaf); the profile’s initialization, input, and (where claimed) progress conditions hold.
  • Preservation gate. Every protected obligation in the previous version’s effective inventory remains active with the same semantic content, or an authorized disposition records its retirement or weakening. A support, ownership, or interpretation edit that deactivates a protected obligation is rejected.

The separation matters. A failing behavioral check does not remove the intent from AAA (Lemma 2). A failing provenance check does not silently delete a machine. A support-only edit cannot deactivate a protected obligation without a disposition (condition 7). All failures are reported with their obligations, their evidence status, and the relevant witnesses. The version is not published until all three gates pass.

4.7 What the gate guarantees

Section titled “4.7 What the gate guarantees”

The gate guarantees that the published executable system refines the active root intents under the declared observation profile and substrate semantics. The guarantee is conditional on validity conditions 5 and 6 (executable realization and profile admissibility) and on the preservation condition 7, and it is relative to:

  • the admitted root intents and their authority;
  • the semantic profile and the environment assumptions;
  • the soundness of the evidence checkers;
  • the connector admissibility proofs;
  • the declared execution semantics of the leaf programs.

These are the theorem’s hypotheses, not disclaimers. The next section makes the composition conditions explicit.

5. Decomposition and Interaction

Section titled “5. Decomposition and Interaction”

5.1 Contracts are relational

Section titled “5.1 Contracts are relational”

A contract that constrains each child separately cannot express a correlation between children. The canonical witness is a parent that admits only the diagonal outcomes.

Proposition 1 (Coordinate projections erase correlation). Let the parent admit the outcome set R={(0,0),(1,1)}R = \{(0,0), (1,1)\}R={(0,0),(1,1)} over outputs (x,y)(x,y)(x,y). The coordinate projections are π1(R)={0,1}\pi_1(R) = \{0,1\}π1​(R)={0,1} and π2(R)={0,1}\pi_2(R) = \{0,1\}π2​(R)={0,1}. Two children that independently refine the projections can jointly emit (0,1)∉R(0,1) \notin R(0,1)∈/R.

Proof. {0,1}×{0,1}\{0,1\} \times \{0,1\}{0,1}×{0,1} contains (0,1)(0,1)(0,1), which is not in RRR. ■\blacksquare■

The remedy is one of two moves: make the contract relational (a relation between child observations and shared connector state), or hoist the correlation into the connector’s wiring. The calculus supports both. The point is that the parent cell must own the correlation; it cannot be pushed into independent child proofs.

5.2 Sibling independence

Section titled “5.2 Sibling independence”

Theorem 2 (Sibling independence). Fix a parent cell v∈Vv \in Vv∈V with children ch⁡(v)\operatorname{ch}(v)ch(v), contracts (Bv,c)c∈ch⁡(v)(B_{v,c})_{c \in \operatorname{ch}(v)}(Bv,c​)c∈ch(v)​, wiring WvW_vWv​, and parent machine MvM_vMv​. Suppose:

  2. Connector monotonicity. The transformer KvK_vKv​ induced by WvW_vWv​ is monotone.
  3. Decomposition. Kv({beh⁡(Bv,c)}c)⊆beh⁡(Mv)K_v(\{\operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c})\}_c) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_v)Kv​({beh(Bv,c​)}c​)⊆beh(Mv​).
  4. Applicability. The wiring’s operational realization is sound for KvK_vKv​; interaction ownership and reduction preservation hold as required by the profile.

Then

Kv({αv,c(beh⁡(Mc))}c)⊆beh⁡(Mv),K_v\bigl(\{\alpha_{v,c}(\operatorname{beh}(M_c))\}_c\bigr) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_v),Kv​({αv,c​(beh(Mc​))}c​)⊆beh(Mv​),

without constructing the concrete sibling product ∏cSMc\prod_c S_{M_c}∏c​SMc​​.

Proof. Apply the abstraction maps to the child refinements, then apply monotonicity to get Kv({αv,c(beh⁡(Mc))}c)⊆Kv({beh⁡(Bv,c)}c)K_v(\{\alpha_{v,c}(\operatorname{beh}(M_c))\}_c) \subseteq K_v(\{\operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c})\}_c)Kv​({αv,c​(beh(Mc​))}c​)⊆Kv​({beh(Bv,c​)}c​), and compose with the decomposition. ■\blacksquare■

The theorem is the step case of Theorem 1, stated separately because it is the engineering claim. The children are verified against their contracts, never against each other. The cost of the parent check is the abstract boundary, not the concrete product.

5.3 Executable closure

Section titled “5.3 Executable closure”

A connector that performs stateful coordination cannot remain an unimplemented mathematical object. The calculus requires:

  • the wiring WvW_vWv​ owns only the specified composition mechanism: routing, synchronizing, interleaving, hiding;
  • any stateful coordinator is a child cell with its own machine, contract, and eventual realization;
  • any custom router, scheduler, or runtime adapter introduced by the implementation receives its own realization obligation or becomes an explicit substrate assumption;
  • no action disappears between the mathematical composition and the executable delivery.

This rule closes the gap that otherwise lets an agent write a beautiful abstract connector and never implement it. The coordinator is refined like everything else.

5.4 Shared services

Section titled “5.4 Shared services”

A service used by several branches in the DAG is declared at a selected common dominating ancestor u∈Dom⁡(c)u \in \operatorname{Dom}(c)u∈Dom(c) as an abstract atomic contract OabsO^{\mathrm{abs}}Oabs in the ambient context. Here, the dominator set is defined as:

Dom⁡(c)={ u∈V  ∣  ∀ directed path π from any root r∈Vroot to c, u∈π }.\operatorname{Dom}(c) = \bigl\{\, u \in V \;\big|\; \forall \text{ directed path } \pi \text{ from any root } r \in V_{\mathrm{root}} \text{ to } c,\ u \in \pi \,\bigr\}.Dom(c)={u∈V​∀ directed path π from any root r∈Vroot​ to c, u∈π}.

If the DAG structure lacks an internal common dominator, the shared service is declared at an enclosing ambient root cell r⊤∈Dom⁡(c)r_\top \in \operatorname{Dom}(c)r⊤​∈Dom(c). Clients invoke OabsO^{\mathrm{abs}}Oabs atomically without widening intermediate interfaces. The service is implemented once, as a separate subgraph, and proved to refine OabsO^{\mathrm{abs}}Oabs: linearizability for safety, a progress property for liveness. This is a factoring rule, not a new judgment. A stateless both-mover service (logging, telemetry) is an admissible connector with trivial state; its certificates establish the required commutation and progress.

5.5 Contract factoring and capacity

Section titled “5.5 Contract factoring and capacity”

A contract boundary can move history into the child and keep the connector small. With mmm idempotent resource bits and the invariant “not all mmm are held,” a naive joint recognizer needs 2m2^m2m states. With per-child two-state contracts that emit signed changes only on a genuine bit change, a connector that counts holders needs m+1m+1m+1 states. The gain is architectural: the connector’s state is small, and the history lives in the children. The bound is not a universal polynomial claim; the abstract boundary can still contain a product of contract states when the architecture requires it. The point is to choose the boundary so that the product is small.

5.6 Applicability conditions

Section titled “5.6 Applicability conditions”

The sibling-independence theorem is only as strong as its applicability conditions. The paper states them in the main text because they are the load-bearing assumptions:

  • Interaction ownership. Every shared interaction has an owning boundary; children have disjoint private state.
  • Operational soundness. The wiring model covers actual routing, synchronization, initialization, and shared-resource behavior.
  • Input and progress. The profile’s input receptiveness and progress obligations are preserved by the child refinement.
  • Reduction preservation. When interleavings are reduced, the reduction preserves the observations of the profile.

A connector that fails one of these is outside the calculus. The failure is a proof obligation, not a silent assumption.

5.7 Practical integration recipes for third-party libraries and shared infrastructure

Section titled “5.7 Practical integration recipes for third-party libraries and shared infrastructure”

Real-world software engineering seldom builds systems from bare metal; applications ubiquitously depend on third-party libraries (npm, pip, crates.io), shared databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL), distributed caches (Redis), and message brokers (Kafka). The calculus provides three concrete, practical recipes for integrating these components without forcing teams to formalize external dependencies from scratch:

Recipe 1 — Third-Party Libraries as Substrate Leaf Cells. When an application calls an external library (e.g., cryptographic hashing, compression, HTTP parsing):

  • The library is modeled as a leaf cell ℓlib∈Vleaf\ell_{\mathrm{lib}} \in V_{\mathrm{leaf}}ℓlib​∈Vleaf​ whose interface exposes only the declared call-and-return observation alphabet.
  • The parent declares an abstract contract Bv,libB_{v,\mathrm{lib}}Bv,lib​ specifying only the functional slice invoked by the parent (e.g., sha256(b) returns the correct 32-byte digest; parse_json(s) returns a parsed AST or syntax error). Unused library features remain outside the observation alphabet.
  • Realization beh⁡(Plib)⊆beh⁡(Mlib)\operatorname{beh}(P_{\mathrm{lib}}) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_{\mathrm{lib}})beh(Plib​)⊆beh(Mlib​) and slot refinement αv,lib(beh⁡(Mlib))⊆beh⁡(Bv,lib)\alpha_{v,\mathrm{lib}}(\operatorname{beh}(M_{\mathrm{lib}})) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(B_{v,\mathrm{lib}})αv,lib​(beh(Mlib​))⊆beh(Bv,lib​) are either discharged via a verified implementation certificate in EEE (e.g., HACL*, EverCrypt) or declared as an explicit substrate assumption in context premise ΔPℓlib\Delta P_{\ell_{\mathrm{lib}}}ΔPℓlib​​, rendering the root guarantee conditional on that substrate contract (analogous to fsync in §8.5). The team verifies application code against the contract slice without re-verifying unverified external source.

Recipe 2 — Shared Databases via Admissible-Input Restriction. When an application uses an external relational database:

  • The database interface is modeled as a child cell cdbc_{\mathrm{db}}cdb​.
  • A full relational database accepts arbitrary SQL strings, but parent vvv‘s connector WvW_vWv​ issues only a finite family of parameterized queries Av,dbA_{v,\mathrm{db}}Av,db​ (e.g., INSERT INTO orders ..., SELECT balance FROM accounts WHERE id = ? FOR UPDATE).
  • By §2.2, the edge refinement is restricted to admissible input histories: αv,db(beh⁡(Mdb) ⁣↾Av,db)  ⊆  beh⁡(Bv,db).\alpha_{v,\mathrm{db}}\bigl(\operatorname{beh}(M_{\mathrm{db}})\!\upharpoonright_{A_{v,\mathrm{db}}}\bigr) \;\subseteq\; \operatorname{beh}(B_{v,\mathrm{db}}).αv,db​(beh(Mdb​)↾Av,db​​)⊆beh(Bv,db​).
  • The parent wiring satisfies the admissible-input delivery premise, ensuring queries outside Av,dbA_{v,\mathrm{db}}Av,db​ cannot be emitted. The contract Bv,dbB_{v,\mathrm{db}}Bv,db​ formalizes only the table schema, serializable transaction semantics, and failure outcomes (e.g., unique key violation, deadlock retry), abstracting the underlying database engine (whose conformance to MdbM_{\mathrm{db}}Mdb​ on Av,dbA_{v,\mathrm{db}}Av,db​ is either certified against a formal engine model in EEE or recorded as an explicit substrate assumption in ΔPcdb\Delta P_{c_{\mathrm{db}}}ΔPcdb​​).

Recipe 3 — Shared Stateful Infrastructure and Dominating Ancestors. When multiple parallel subsystems share a single runtime singleton (e.g., a shared connection pool, rate limiter, or distributed lock):

  • Independent per-child contracts cannot soundly express correlated shared-state side effects (Proposition 1 and Proposition 2).
  • The shared singleton is scoped at a common dominating ancestor u∈Dom⁡(c)u \in \operatorname{Dom}(c)u∈Dom(c) (or at enclosing ambient root r⊤r_\topr⊤​) via an abstract atomic contract OabsO^{\mathrm{abs}}Oabs (§5.4).
  • Intermediate clients interact through private session handles. The dominating ancestor’s connector owns the multi-client interleaving, and linearizability or serializability certificates discharge sibling non-interference. Sibling modules remain independently verifiable within their local contracts.

6. The Development Protocol

Section titled “6. The Development Protocol”

6.1 The five gates

Section titled “6.1 The five gates”

The protocol is the operational reading of validity. An agent may publish a version only when all five gates pass.

G1 — Read the context (process duty). Before proposing a change at a cell vvv, the agent reads the cell’s context premises ΔPv\Delta P_vΔPv​, its active intents A(v)A(v)A(v), support links JJJ, incoming contracts, outgoing decomposition χ(v)\chi(v)χ(v), and the cut/subgraph view in which vvv participates. This is a process obligation on the agent; G2–G5 are checked by the gate.

G2 — No abstraction skip. A machine at child cell ccc is introduced only as a child of a contract already declared in some decomposition record χ(v)\chi(v)χ(v). The agent cannot write leaf code without first fixing the contract it must satisfy. This is the direct block on the wide abstraction leap.

G3 — Evidence required. Acceptance of a cell requires valid satisfaction evidence for every active intent assigned to it and valid executable-realization evidence: for a non-leaf cell, the universal wiring-adequacy certificate of condition 5; for a leaf, the program-to-machine inclusion. A non-leaf cell also requires valid decomposition evidence. Acceptance of a decomposition edge requires valid child refinement evidence. A test is evidence only for the claim it can establish. A weakened test weakens the claim, not the obligation; the universal obligation remains active and unsatisfied.

G4 — No silent specification weakening. Root and protected intents and contracts can be changed only through an authorized revision that creates a new version and reopens the dependent context premises. The agent may propose a revision; it cannot apply one as part of a code change. A support, ownership, or interpretation edit that deactivates a protected obligation counts as a specification weakening and requires an authorized disposition. The authorization record is part of the version.

G5 — Atomic publication. A version is published only when every obligation in the affected dependency cone has valid pass evidence. Incomplete subgraphs are not publishable. Missing, unresolved, or pending evidence is not a pass, and a failed local verification cannot be hidden by a successful build elsewhere.

6.2 The authoring cycle

Section titled “6.2 The authoring cycle”

The agent’s authoring cycle is:

  1. Read. Load the cell’s cut inspection view and incoming slot contracts.
  2. Context. For each cell, record context premises ΔPv\Delta P_vΔPv​ with upstream dependencies, alternatives, rationale, and reopening conditions. An edit that changes a protected item requires an authorized revision.
  3. Model. Propose the cell’s machine MvM_vMv​. The machine must satisfy the active intents assigned to the cell.
  4. Decompose. For an internal cell, declare the wiring skeleton and child contracts, and discharge the decomposition and wiring-adequacy obligations.
  5. Assign. Hand each child contract to the child cell. The child may be developed independently within its contract.
  6. Substitute. When a child is complete, substitute its refinement proof into the parent’s decomposition. Close the parent only when all child edges are discharged.

A locally checked design with unresolved descendants remains a development candidate. The completed-system gate quantifies over all required cells, decompositions, and executable artifacts.

6.3 What the agent may and may not change

Section titled “6.3 What the agent may and may not change”
Artifact Agent may Agent may not
Delegated intent refine, strengthen, add a child intent, or retire with recorded rationale in version provenance weaken a parent-assigned boundary contract or protected obligation without an authorized revision
Protected intent propose a revision with rationale and reopening apply the revision, downgrade its authority, or deactivate it via a support/ownership edit, without an authorized disposition
Root intent implement it silently weaken, reinterpret, or deactivate it
Contract refine the child implementation; propose a contract revision change the contract to make a failing child pass
Context premise add, re-warrant, or reopen with rationale erase the alternatives or the rationale
Machine choose any implementation within the contract declare a contract that the parent decomposition does not support
Evidence add evidence for the exact obligation substitute a weaker claim for a stronger obligation

6.4 Test weakening, intent revision, and authority

Section titled “6.4 Test weakening, intent revision, and authority”

The test-weakening failure is blocked by the evidence discipline. A test is a decision procedure for a bounded or sampled claim. It cannot discharge a universal inclusion unless it is exhaustive for the relevant finite domain. If the agent deletes an assertion, the remaining test establishes a weaker claim; the universal obligation is still active, and the gate reports it as unsatisfied. The only way to remove the obligation is to change its intent, which requires an authorized revision and reopens the dependent context premises. A support, ownership, or interpretation edit that removes a protected obligation is a removal even when the predicate bytes are unchanged; it requires the same authorized disposition.

The authority tags make this concrete:

  • Root intents are admitted by the owner at version creation.
  • Protected intents and contracts require an explicit authorization record to change.
  • Delegated intents may be refined by the agent within the protected boundary.

The authorization record is not a separate governance mechanism. It is a field of the version, checked by the same gate.

6.5 A transcript of a caught error

Section titled “6.5 A transcript of a caught error”
  1. The requirement says: acknowledge a request only after its result is durable.
  2. The agent writes a store that emits committed after write returns.
  3. The refinement check for the store contract returns the trace append, committed with no flush_ok/fsync.
  4. The evidence record is fail. The store contract remains active.
  5. The agent either adds the flush before committed (downward repair at the leaf program) or, if the substrate cannot support the required durability, introduces a supported flush protocol and implements it, or obtains an authorized revision of the substrate/requirement premise and reopens the store decomposition.
  6. The version is published only after the new evidence passes and the reopen path is recorded.

The next section gives the full example.

7.2 Contextual intent projection and property-driven refinement

Section titled “7.2 Contextual intent projection and property-driven refinement”

When a requirement evolves or a new capability is introduced, intent propagation proceeds top-down along the DAG from roots through successive child edges. At each step, an agent refines an incoming component requirement by decomposing it into sibling contracts under local domain premises.

Definition (Contextual Intent Projection). Let cell v∈V(t)v \in V^{(t)}v∈V(t) have an active component requirement Rv⊆OXvR_v \subseteq \mathcal{O}_{X_v}Rv​⊆OXv​​ and local context premises ΔPv\Delta P_vΔPv​ (encapsulating domain axioms, maintained state invariants, or declared workload conditions). A decomposition χt+1(v)=(Wt+1,v,ch⁡t+1(v),(Bt+1,v,c,αt+1,v,c)c∈ch⁡t+1(v))\chi_{t+1}(v) = \bigl(W_{t+1,v}, \operatorname{ch}_{t+1}(v), (B_{t+1,v,c}, \alpha_{t+1,v,c})_{c \in \operatorname{ch}_{t+1}(v)}\bigr)χt+1​(v)=(Wt+1,v​,cht+1​(v),(Bt+1,v,c​,αt+1,v,c​)c∈cht+1​(v)​) is a valid contextual projection of RvR_vRv​ under ΔPv\Delta P_vΔPv​ iff

ΔPv  ⟹  KWt+1,v({beh⁡(Bt+1,v,c)}c∈ch⁡t+1(v))⊆Rv.\Delta P_v \implies K_{W_{t+1,v}}\Bigl(\bigl\{\operatorname{beh}(B_{t+1,v,c})\bigr\}_{c \in \operatorname{ch}_{t+1}(v)}\Bigr) \subseteq R_v .ΔPv​⟹KWt+1,v​​({beh(Bt+1,v,c​)}c∈cht+1​(v)​)⊆Rv​.

Residual Conservation Law. The child contracts {Bt+1,v,c}c∈ch⁡t+1(v)\{B_{t+1,v,c}\}_{c \in \operatorname{ch}_{t+1}(v)}{Bt+1,v,c​}c∈cht+1​(v)​ are the residual obligations passed down to children. When cell vvv extracts no intermediate abstraction, the projection is the identity pass-through Bt+1,v,c=RvB_{t+1,v,c} = R_vBt+1,v,c​=Rv​ with a single child. The inclusion guarantees conservation of intent across abstraction boundaries: an agent cannot satisfy an abstract goal by relaxing a binding mechanism requirement without explicitly discharging the residual constraint in the child cells.

Maintained behavioral invariants are enforced as subset inclusions across sibling contracts and connector wiring, whereas environmental and workload premises are recorded in ΔPv\Delta P_vΔPv​. If operational workload or environment assumptions shift, premise ΔPv\Delta P_vΔPv​ becomes stale, triggering targeted reopening of the local decomposition without invalidating orthogonal verified components.
