7.4 Implementation remark: persistent outgoing-edge containers

Section titled “7.4 Implementation remark: persistent outgoing-edge containers”

In an executable repository or development environment, version-indexed decompositions χt(v)\chi_t(v)χt​(v) are realized without copying entire tree spines by maintaining a persistent array or persistent linked list of outgoing decomposition entries at each cell, with a fixed sentinel root r⊤r_\topr⊤​ above VrootV_{\mathrm{root}}Vroot​:

  • Localized update. Updating a region at version t+1t+1t+1 appends a new versioned entry (t+1,χt+1(v))(t+1, \chi_{t+1}(v))(t+1,χt+1​(v)) to the upper-boundary parent’s persistent container. Unchanged ancestors and sibling subtrees remain shared by pointer identity without cloning.
  • Rollback and Historical Inspection. Reverting a sub-development region to a historical checkpoint s<ts < ts<t appends (t+1,χs(v))(t+1, \chi_s(v))(t+1,χs​(v)) across the cells of the reverted region (or records an explicit snapshot override snap=s\mathrm{snap} = ssnap=s on the reverted boundary entry). Reading a cell at epoch TTT selects the newest entry with write epoch t≤Tt \le Tt≤T (or evaluates the reverted sub-DAG at epoch sss when following an explicit snapshot override snap=s\mathrm{snap} = ssnap=s).

7.5 The evolution loop

Section titled “7.5 The evolution loop”

The evolution function

Gt+1=evolve⁡(Gt,ΔI)G_{t+1} = \operatorname{evolve}(G_t, \Delta I)Gt+1​=evolve(Gt​,ΔI)

computes a candidate development from an accepted delta ΔI\Delta IΔI, returning Verified, Conflict, or Unresolved. There is no default-to-pass.

Step 1 — Apply and reactivate. Apply ΔI\Delta IΔI: a new root intent, an updated context premise, an authorized revision, or a contract adjustment. Recompute active intents AAA via topological support evaluation. Evaluate affected context premises ΔPv\Delta P_vΔPv​ against upstream models and verify mutual compatibility. Mark stale components by reachability along ΔPv∗\Delta P_v^*ΔPv∗​. If context premises conflict, return Conflict with the conflicting premises and rationales; stop before initiating machine search.

Step 2 — Locate. Walk the DAG in topological order, evaluating only the newly introduced or modified obligations in the set difference Req⁡(Gt+1)∖Req⁡(Gt)\operatorname{Req}(G_{t+1}) \setminus \operatorname{Req}(G_t)Req(Gt+1​)∖Req(Gt​). The result of each check is one of: pass, fail with a semantic counterexample, failed proof witness (e.g., an inductive invariant or simulation relation that failed), or unresolved (timeout or resource exhaustion). Let jjj be the first cell at which an obligation does not pass. Publish only when every required obligation in Req⁡(Gt+1)∖Req⁡(Gt)\operatorname{Req}(G_{t+1}) \setminus \operatorname{Req}(G_t)Req(Gt+1​)∖Req(Gt​) has valid pass evidence.

Step 3 — Repair at jjj. The check result determines the repair strategy:

  • Semantic counterexample, genuine. A concrete execution admitted by cell jjj‘s machine violates an active intent, or a concrete interleaving of child contracts violates the decomposition. Repair the machine, connector, or contracts at cell jjj; re-establish its obligations and upward refinement; propagate upward along the affected spine.
  • Semantic counterexample, spurious child refinement. The child’s model or abstraction overapproximates: it admits behavior the fixed child implementation cannot produce. Repair the child model or its abstraction map by narrowing the abstraction, and re-establish the lower realization and upper refinement. Narrowing the parent-side contract for a fixed child abstraction makes the inclusion harder and cannot remove the spurious behavior.
  • Semantic counterexample, spurious decomposition. The parent-side child contract is too permissive and the concrete children satisfy a stronger contract. Narrow the parent-side child contract or repair the connector, and re-establish the decomposition. If the concrete children do not satisfy the stronger contract, the repair belongs to the children.
  • Failed proof witness. An inductive invariant or simulation relation failed. Strengthen or repair the witness and recheck. This is a proof-search outcome, not a semantic counterexample and not a machine edit by itself.
  • Unresolved. The checker timed out or returned unknown. Return Unresolved; do not classify as genuine or spurious, and do not publish.

For a refinement failure, the discrete set example is decisive: implementation {ok}\{ok\}{ok}, child abstraction {ok,bad}\{ok,bad\}{ok,bad}, parent contract {ok}\{ok\}{ok}. The implementation satisfies the contract, but the abstraction admits badbadbad. No stronger parent contract repairs the fixed child abstraction; narrowing the child abstraction to {ok}\{ok\}{ok} does. A child refinement failure is never repaired by strengthening the parent-side contract alone.

The genuine/spurious test for a semantic decomposition counterexample uses one shared trajectory:

∃r. legal⁡Wv(r) ∧ obs⁡v(r)=τ ∧ ∀c∈ch⁡(v). realizable⁡v,c(Mc,slice⁡c(r)),\exists r.\ \operatorname{legal}_{W_v}(r) \ \wedge\ \operatorname{obs}_v(r) = \tau \ \wedge\ \forall c \in \operatorname{ch}(v).\ \operatorname{realizable}_{v,c}\bigl(M_c, \operatorname{slice}_c(r)\bigr),∃r. legalWv​​(r) ∧ obsv​(r)=τ ∧ ∀c∈ch(v). realizablev,c​(Mc​,slicec​(r)),

where realizable⁡v,c(Mc,o)  ⟺  o∈αv,c(beh⁡(Mc) ⁣↾Av,c)\operatorname{realizable}_{v,c}(M_c, o) \iff o \in \alpha_{v,c}(\operatorname{beh}(M_c)\!\upharpoonright_{A_{v,c}})realizablev,c​(Mc​,o)⟺o∈αv,c​(beh(Mc​)↾Av,c​​) means that slot observation slice o∈OXv,co \in \mathcal{O}_{X_{v,c}}o∈OXv,c​​ is the edge-abstraction image of an admissible child execution of McM_cMc​. A separate existential trajectory per child is not sufficient: two children can each be realizable on their own slice while no common trajectory exists. The shared-bit witness is Proposition 2.

Step 4 — Publish. If every obligation in Req⁡(Gt+1)∖Req⁡(Gt)\operatorname{Req}(G_{t+1}) \setminus \operatorname{Req}(G_t)Req(Gt+1​)∖Req(Gt​) has valid pass evidence and every load-bearing context premise is warranted, atomically install Gt+1G_{t+1}Gt+1​ and record authorization At+1\mathcal{A}_{t+1}At+1​. Otherwise return Unresolved with the failing or unresolved obligations and their witnesses.

7.6 Genuine vs. spurious

Section titled “7.6 Genuine vs. spurious”

Proposition 2 (Separate realizations do not imply a joint realization). There are two child contracts, one requiring a shared bit (fixed per trajectory) to be 000 and one requiring it to be 111, such that each is separately realizable but no common trajectory realizes both.

Proof. Let each trajectory carry a single fixed shared bit value b∈{0,1}b \in \{0,1\}b∈{0,1}. Child 1 is realizable only with b=0b = 0b=0; child 2 is realizable only with b=1b = 1b=1. Each existential check succeeds with a different value of bbb. No single trajectory rrr has both b=0b = 0b=0 and b=1b = 1b=1. ■\blacksquare■

The proposition is the reason the repair step uses a joint trajectory. It is also the reason a connector that hides shared state behind per-child contracts is unsound: the correlation is not in either contract.

7.7 Staleness and reopening

Section titled “7.7 Staleness and reopening”

A change to an intent, contract, or context premise activates its dependency cone along ΔPv∗\Delta P_v^*ΔPv∗​. Every cell in the cone is stale until re-warranted. A reopened design alternative becomes selectable again under updated context premises; selecting it creates an updated decomposition with its own context and evidence. Prior versions remain in the history {Gt}\{G_t\}{Gt​}, preserving the audit trail.

The dependency cone is computed on the reference graph of semantic operands, not on physical storage pointers. An internal implementation change with an unchanged semantic contract does not activate the cone. This is the practical benefit of grounding obligations directly in semantic proposition identity: unchanged boundaries immediately prune propagation, keeping the verified blast radius strictly localized to the modified subgraph.

8. End-to-End Example: Durable Acknowledgement

Section titled “8. End-to-End Example: Durable Acknowledgement”

8.1 The requirement and scope

Section titled “8.1 The requirement and scope”

The system instance serves one request. The environment precondition is: at most one req(id) is delivered to an instance, and the instance is not reused after ack or fail. A reusable service needs a reset transition and matching contracts; that variant is outside this example.

The declared safety intent is:

  • Safety. For every identifier ididid, an ack(id) output occurs only after the result for ididid is durable, witnessed at the store boundary by flush_ok(id) before committed(id).

The liveness claim is separate and conditional:

  • Conditional liveness. If the scheduler is fair, the store responds to every append(id) with flush_ok(id) or flush_fail(id), and the coordinator is fair, then every req(id) is eventually followed by ack(id) or fail(id).

The safety proof does not establish conditional liveness. Liveness is discharged only under those premises, which are recorded in the profile of the coordinator and store cells. The leaf runtime is run-to-completion, non-reentrant, with a FIFO event queue: emit enqueues an event and returns; the current handler completes before the next event is dispatched. Initialization is coordinator state idle and store state empty. The reentrant interpretation is outside this example; §8.5 also places the coordinator in appending before append is emitted, so a reentrant response is not discarded.

The architecture is a two-level Refinement DAG: root cell v0v_0v0​ decomposes into children ch⁡(v0)={coord,store}\operatorname{ch}(v_0) = \{\mathrm{coord}, \mathrm{store}\}ch(v0​)={coord,store}, both of which are leaf cells (ch⁡(coord)=ch⁡(store)=∅\operatorname{ch}(\mathrm{coord}) = \operatorname{ch}(\mathrm{store}) = \emptysetch(coord)=ch(store)=∅) realized directly by executable programs PcoordP_{\mathrm{coord}}Pcoord​ and PstoreP_{\mathrm{store}}Pstore​.

8.2 Root cell: the abstract design

Section titled “8.2 Root cell: the abstract design”

The root cell v0v_0v0​ has the machine M0M_0M0​:

  • states: idle, pending(id), durable(id), acked(id);
  • transitions:
    • idle --req(id)--> pending(id);
    • pending(id) --commit_ok(id)--> durable(id);
    • pending(id) --commit_fail(id)--> acked(id) with output fail(id);
    • durable(id) --tau--> acked(id) with output ack(id).

The root has no transition out of acked(id); the instance is single-use, matching the environment precondition. The machine satisfies the safety intent by construction: ack(id) is emitted only from durable(id), which is reached only by commit_ok(id). Conditional liveness is a separate obligation under the fairness premises; it is not inferred from this safety construction.

The root context premises ΔPv0\Delta P_{v_0}ΔPv0​​ record why the design separates durability from acknowledgement: the alternative of acknowledging on enqueue was rejected because it treats a volatile queue as durable; the reopening condition is a substrate that provides a durable atomic enqueue.

8.3 Root decomposition

Section titled “8.3 Root decomposition”

The root cell v0v_0v0​ declares two children: a coordinator coord and a durable store store. The wiring W0W_0W0​ routes:

  • req(id) from the environment to coord;
  • append(id) from coord to store;
  • committed(id) and failed(id) from store to coord;
  • ack(id) and fail(id) from coord to the environment.

The store’s boundary also exposes flush_ok(id) and flush_fail(id); the wiring routes them to the environment observer that witnesses durability. The root’s commit_ok is the abstraction of the store’s flush_ok followed by committed; the abstraction map α\alphaα is part of the decomposition record.

The contracts are:

B0,coordB_{0,\mathrm{coord}}B0,coord​ — inputs req(id), committed(id), failed(id); outputs append(id), ack(id), fail(id). Duties: at most one req(id) per instance; no second request after ack or fail; append(id) may follow req(id); ack(id) only after committed(id); fail(id) only after failed(id). Conditional progress: under fair coordinator scheduling and a store response, every req(id) eventually receives ack(id) or fail(id).

B0,storeB_{0,\mathrm{store}}B0,store​ — inputs append(id); observable outputs flush_ok(id), flush_fail(id), committed(id), failed(id). Duties: at most one append(id) per instance; committed(id) only after flush_ok(id); flush_ok(id) is the substrate’s durability event; failed(id) only after flush_fail(id). Conditional progress: under the substrate’s fairness, every append(id) eventually receives flush_ok(id) or flush_fail(id) and then committed(id) or failed(id).

The contracts are not merely necessary ordering duties. Their trace languages are the prefix closures (where pref⁡(L)={u∣∃w. uw∈L}\operatorname{pref}(L) = \{u \mid \exists w.\ uw \in L\}pref(L)={u∣∃w. uw∈L} denotes the prefix closure of trace set LLL), with one identifier per instance, alongside the root machine’s trace language L0L_0L0​:

Lcoord=pref⁡(req(id) append(id) committed(id) ack(id))∪pref⁡(req(id) append(id) failed(id) fail(id)),Lstore=pref⁡(append(id) flush_ok(id) committed(id))∪pref⁡(append(id) flush_fail(id) failed(id)),L0=pref⁡(req(id) commit_ok(id) ack(id))∪pref⁡(req(id) commit_fail(id) fail(id)).\begin{aligned} L_{\mathrm{coord}} &= \operatorname{pref}(\texttt{req}(id)\,\texttt{append}(id)\,\texttt{committed}(id)\,\texttt{ack}(id)) \cup \operatorname{pref}(\texttt{req}(id)\,\texttt{append}(id)\,\texttt{failed}(id)\,\texttt{fail}(id)), \\ L_{\mathrm{store}} &= \operatorname{pref}(\texttt{append}(id)\,\texttt{flush\_ok}(id)\,\texttt{committed}(id)) \cup \operatorname{pref}(\texttt{append}(id)\,\texttt{flush\_fail}(id)\,\texttt{failed}(id)), \\ L_0 &= \operatorname{pref}(\texttt{req}(id)\,\texttt{commit\_ok}(id)\,\texttt{ack}(id)) \cup \operatorname{pref}(\texttt{req}(id)\,\texttt{commit\_fail}(id)\,\texttt{fail}(id)). \end{aligned}Lcoord​Lstore​L0​​=pref(req(id)append(id)committed(id)ack(id))∪pref(req(id)append(id)failed(id)fail(id)),=pref(append(id)flush_ok(id)committed(id))∪pref(append(id)flush_fail(id)failed(id)),=pref(req(id)commit_ok(id)ack(id))∪pref(req(id)commit_fail(id)fail(id)).​

The prefix closure ends at ack or fail; a second ack, a spontaneous output, or an incompatible continuation is not in LcoordL_{\mathrm{coord}}Lcoord​. The duplicate-ack composition trace req, append, flush_ok, committed, ack, ack projects onto the coordinator alphabet as req, append, committed, ack, ack, which is not in the prefix closure LcoordL_{\mathrm{coord}}Lcoord​; the composition trace is therefore excluded by the contract.

The store boundary observation alphabet explicitly includes flush_ok and flush_fail. The proof boundary is not the projection that hides them: hiding flush_ok would make the good trace append, flush_ok, committed and the bad trace append, committed indistinguishable, so the durability duty would not be checkable. The contract keeps the durability observation visible.

The decomposition obligation is K0(beh⁡(B0,coord),beh⁡(B0,store))⊆beh⁡(M0)K_0(\operatorname{beh}(B_{0,\mathrm{coord}}), \operatorname{beh}(B_{0,\mathrm{store}})) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_0)K0​(beh(B0,coord​),beh(B0,store​))⊆beh(M0​). It holds for the single-use protocol: any composition trace is a one-request trace; its ack is preceded by the coordinator’s committed, which is preceded by the store’s flush_ok; the root’s commit_ok/ack path matches. The commit_fail/fail path matches the store’s flush_fail/failed and the coordinator’s fail. The abstraction maps the composition trace req, append, flush_ok, committed, ack to req, commit_ok, ack and req, append, flush_fail, failed, fail to req, commit_fail, fail; the composition’s trace language is contained in L0L_0L0​. The two-request trace req(1), append(1), flush_ok(1), committed(1), ack(1), req(2), ... is excluded by the interface precondition and the one-request trace language. The duplicate-ack trace req, append, flush_ok, committed, ack, ack is excluded by the prefix closure LcoordL_{\mathrm{coord}}Lcoord​. The wiring is stateless; the coordinator is a child cell, not an oracle inside the connector.

8.4 Child machines

Section titled “8.4 Child machines”

Coordinator McoordM_{\mathrm{coord}}Mcoord​: states idle, appending(id), ready(id), done(id).

  • idle --req(id)--> appending(id) with output append(id);
  • appending(id) --committed(id)--> ready(id);
  • ready(id) --tau--> done(id) with output ack(id);
  • appending(id) --failed(id)--> done(id) with output fail(id).

Its local active intent is “no acknowledgement before a committed result.” The refinement Mcoord⪯B0,coordM_{\mathrm{coord}} \preceq B_{0,\mathrm{coord}}Mcoord​⪯B0,coord​ is a short simulation: ack only from ready, which is reached only by committed; the one-request clause follows from the absence of a transition out of done, and the trace language is exactly LcoordL_{\mathrm{coord}}Lcoord​.

Store MstoreM_{\mathrm{store}}Mstore​: states empty, writing(id), flushed(id), committed(id), failed.

  • empty --append(id)--> writing(id);
  • writing(id) --flush_ok(id)--> flushed(id);
  • flushed(id) --tau--> committed(id) with output committed(id);
  • writing(id) --flush_fail(id)--> failed with output failed(id).
  • committed(id) has no outgoing transition except a silent stutter with no output.

Its local active intent is “committed implies durable.” The refinement Mstore⪯B0,storeM_{\mathrm{store}} \preceq B_{0,\mathrm{store}}Mstore​⪯B0,store​ requires that committed is reachable only after flush_ok, and that flush_ok is the substrate’s durability event. The boundary trace is append, flush_ok, committed (or append, flush_fail, failed); committed is emitted only after flush_ok, and the trace language is exactly LstoreL_{\mathrm{store}}Lstore​.

The context premises record the choice of a write-ahead log over an in-memory queue with periodic snapshots. The premises are the durability requirement and the crash model. The rejected alternative’s reopening condition is “a durable atomic append primitive is available from the substrate.” The context premise is provenance; the behavioral obligation is the refinement of the contracts.

8.5 Executable leaves

Section titled “8.5 Executable leaves”

Both coord and store are leaf cells (ch⁡(coord)=ch⁡(store)=∅\operatorname{ch}(\mathrm{coord}) = \operatorname{ch}(\mathrm{store}) = \emptysetch(coord)=ch(store)=∅) whose executable realization is given directly by programs:

The substrate contract is: fsync returns 0 iff the record is durable across the modeled crash; flush_ok(id) is emitted only on a 0 return. The realization witness for the store relates the log state to MstoreM_{\mathrm{store}}Mstore​‘s state: fsync success corresponds to the flush_ok transition, and the committed emission corresponds to flushed -> committed. The invariant is “a record is in flushed only if the corresponding fsync returned 0.” The good trace append, flush_ok, committed is admitted; the bad trace append, committed is not, because no flush_ok transition occurred. The coordinator realization is the analogous event-loop simulation; ack is emitted on the ready -> done transition, after committed. Under the declared run-to-completion semantics, the response cannot be delivered while the request handler is still running; the program also enters appending before emitting append, so a synchronous/reentrant response would find the handler in appending and would not be discarded. Under the declared semantics and the stated fairness/enabling premises, the coordinator reaches done and emits ack; this is the conditional liveness claim, not part of the safety realization.

8.6 The agent’s initial mistake

Section titled “8.6 The agent’s initial mistake”

The agent writes the store to emit committed immediately after write returns, before fsync. The refinement check Pstore⪯MstoreP_{\mathrm{store}} \preceq M_{\mathrm{store}}Pstore​⪯Mstore​ fails with the finite trace append(id), committed(id)\texttt{append}(id),\ \texttt{committed}(id)append(id), committed(id). The trace violates the durability duty: committed occurs without flush_ok. The evidence record is fail, and the store contract remains active.

Two repairs are available.

  • Downward repair at the leaf. Add the fsync before committed. The new store program satisfies the same contract. Only the store’s leaf realization obligation Impl⁡(store)\operatorname{Impl}(\mathrm{store})Impl(store) changes. The leaf machine MstoreM_{\mathrm{store}}Mstore​ and its incoming contract B0,storeB_{0,\mathrm{store}}B0,store​ are fixed (with identity edge abstraction α0,store\alpha_{0,\mathrm{store}}α0,store​ matching MstoreM_{\mathrm{store}}Mstore​ to B0,storeB_{0,\mathrm{store}}B0,store​), so Ref⁡(v0,store)\operatorname{Ref}(v_0, \mathrm{store})Ref(v0​,store) and the parent Dec⁡(v0)\operatorname{Dec}(v_0)Dec(v0​) are unchanged. By Corollary 2 (Interface Cutoff), the parent decomposition and coordinator proofs are reused without solver re-execution.
  • Upward refinement. Strengthening a contract cannot make an incapable substrate provide durability. The upward path is one of two authorized changes: (i) introduce a supported flush protocol and implement it, with the new contract and evidence; or (ii) revise the substrate or requirement premise with an authorized disposition and reopen the store decomposition. The example assumes the substrate supports fsync; the upward path is for a different substrate and must be authorized and re-verified.

The version history records both paths and the condition under which the upward path is preferred. The audit trail is not rewritten: the original failed attempt, its counterexample, and the chosen repair remain in the version history.

8.7 Inspection views via cuts

Section titled “8.7 Inspection views via cuts”

The DAG structure permits human inspection through its natural root-covering cuts:

Cut Cut Antichain CCC What the human sees What they do not need to read
C0C_0C0​ {v0}\{v_0\}{v0​} the safety intent, conditional liveness premise, abstract durability state machine, context premises any component implementation
C1C_1C1​ {coord,store}\{\mathrm{coord}, \mathrm{store}\}{coord,store} coordinator and store machines, contracts including visible flush_ok durability observation, context premises, evidence status the log buffer code

At cut C1C_1C1​, the human can verify the acknowledgement protocol: ack only after committed, committed only after a durable flush, and the progress duties. At the leaves, they audit the program whose contract they already understand. Corollary 1 (Pointwise and Frontier Soundness) guarantees that the cut C1C_1C1​ view is a sound abstraction of the code.

8.8 What the example demonstrates

Section titled “8.8 What the example demonstrates”

The example exercises all three failure modes:

  • the wide leap is blocked because the coordinator and store interfaces must be declared before their code;
  • the rationale is preserved in the context premises, and the rejected in-memory alternative has a reopening condition;
  • the human inspects cut C1C_1C1​ rather than the WAL code.

It also exercises the downward repair and the authorized upward path, and the incremental frame cutoff theorem.

9. Mechanization Target

Section titled “9. Mechanization Target”

The calculus is designed to be mechanized in a small dependent-type development. The target is not a proof of the entire engineering stack; it is a kernel-checked proof of the algebraic spine, with the operational and solver obligations as explicit hypotheses.

9.1 Checked Lean 4 excerpt

Section titled “9.1 Checked Lean 4 excerpt”

The checked formalization in JirlCalculus.lean treats Obs as an arbitrary observation type parameter and proves the algebraic kernel across six sections:

  • Section 1 proves finite-guard and acyclic support-closure lemmas (T_guard, GuardedWitness, EnvClosure, Closure, and joint_support_consistency);
  • Sections 2–5 prove connector monotonicity, compositional sibling independence, joint-trajectory realizability, top-down contextual intent projection (contextual_projection_sound), and the incremental frame theorem (validity_by_reuse, incremental_frame_cutoff, and the Versioned finite snapshot specialization);
  • Section 6 proves typed edge maps with pullback-intersection local property inclusion (pullback_intersection_refinement), heterogeneous cost composition (heterogeneous_composition_with_cost), admissible-input restricted refinement (restricted_refinement_sound and admissible_trajectory_wiring), and well-founded induction for arbitrary finite acyclic child relations (dag_soundness_by_rank) and root-covering cut frontier soundness (frontier_cut_soundness). In RefinementDAG, dag_soundness_by_rank and frontier_cut_soundness mechanize the unrestricted (Av,c=HXcinA_{v,c} = \mathcal{H}_{X_c}^{\mathrm{in}}Av,c​=HXc​in​) full-edge case over per-node behaviors, while restricted_refinement_sound and admissible_trajectory_wiring separately mechanize the admissible-input restricted step.

The formalization also provides concrete witness models in namespaces DAGWitness and EdgeWitness, verifying:

  1. that a DAG with shared leaves reached at unequal path depths satisfies the soundness theorem (unequal_depth_shared_dag_sound);
  2. that a cut that fails to cover all paths from root to leaf admits unsound bypass (bypass_not_root_covering);
  3. that child-local complexity or cost bounds are preserved without inventing spurious parent cost coordinates (heterogeneous_cost_vertical); and
  4. that general-purpose children with wider input domains soundly refine slot contracts under legal parent input trajectories (restricted_input_vertical).

9.2 Trusted base

Section titled “9.2 Trusted base”

The kernel checks the algebra. The following remain explicit hypotheses, with their scopes recorded:

  • the operational soundness of a connector’s wiring against its transformer (the wire premise of dag_soundness_by_rank and frontier_cut_soundness);
  • the aggregate-history adequacy and dominating-ancestor scoping for shared stateful singletons (hypothesis (A4));
  • the soundness of the evidence checker for each method;
  • the adequacy of the finite model to the code for a model-checking claim;
  • the substrate contract for a leaf realization (the leaf / boundary premise);
  • the input-receptiveness and progress obligations for the chosen profile.

A mechanized proof cannot make these hypotheses true. It can make their use explicit and prevent the algebra from hiding them.

9.3 Size

Section titled “9.3 Size”

The mechanized development in JirlCalculus.lean comprises 1,192 lines of Lean 4 with zero sorry tokens and zero custom axioms (relying only on Lean’s standard foundational axioms propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound). The compact size is a design objective: a reader can audit the entire correctness spine in one sitting, and a reviewer can see exactly which premises are assumed.

10. Related Work

Section titled “10. Related Work”

Refinement calculi. Back and von Wright’s refinement calculus and Abrial’s Event-B develop programs by stepwise refinement, with invariants and proof obligations at each step. The refinement-DAG calculus shares the stepwise discipline but makes the interface between nodes a first-class contract and adds a persistent provenance ledger. Event-B’s refinement is per-machine; the DAG calculus adds the connector and the child-contract decomposition, which is what enables independent child verification.

Temporal specification and refinement mappings. TLA+ and the Abadi–Lamport theory of refinement mappings establish implementation relations between specifications. The DAG calculus uses the same inclusion idea, specialized to an acyclic refinement graph with explicit contracts. The connector’s monotonicity is the composition law; the DAG structure is the engineering discipline that keeps the law applicable.

Interface automata and assume-guarantee. de Alfaro and Henzinger’s interface automata formalize open components with input/output variance and compatibility. The child refinement obligation’s input receptiveness is the same discipline. Assume-guarantee reasoning is powerful but fragile when assumptions are circular; the DAG calculus avoids circularity by making the connector own the interaction and by requiring an executable coordinator rather than a circular assumption.

Design by contract. Meyer’s contracts specify preconditions, postconditions, and invariants. The DAG calculus extends the idea from a single object boundary to an acyclic decomposition: the contract is the interface between cells, and its satisfaction is checked by refinement rather than by runtime assertion alone.

Hierarchical state machines. Harel’s statecharts provide nested and orthogonal states. The DAG calculus uses ordinary state machines at each cell and a connector for interaction; it does not rely on statechart semantics. The hierarchy is in the refinement DAG structure, not in a single expanded automaton.

Counterexample-guided abstraction refinement. Clarke et al.’s CEGAR loop uses counterexamples to refine abstractions. The evolution loop is a localized CEGAR: the failure cell localizes the repair, and the shared-trajectory check separates genuine from spurious witnesses. The key difference is that cell contracts are persistent interfaces, so a repair at one cell reuses the proofs at unchanged boundaries.

Truth maintenance and provenance. Truth maintenance systems and provenance semirings model support and retraction. The provenance record borrows the idea of explicit support and reopening: alternatives are preserved with their reopening triggers, and support is strictly acyclic, so the warrant is evaluated in a single forward pass.

Persistent data structures. Driscoll et al. established path copying and persistence. The version model represents evolution as a sequence of immutable Refinement DAGs {Gt}t∈N\{G_t\}_{t \in \mathbb{N}}{Gt​}t∈N​; the incremental frame theorem establishes that unchanged obligation propositions are reused by identity, and persistent outgoing-edge containers provide an efficient store.

Assurance cases and evidential tool buses. Structured assurance cases provide explicit arguments that a critical system satisfies its top-level safety claims, standardized in frameworks such as the Goal Structuring Notation (GSN) [24] and the OMG Structured Assurance Case Metamodel (SACM) [25]. Rushby’s Evidential Tool Bus (ETB) [26] formalizes verification tool interaction as a distributed evidence-producing architecture. Bloomfield and Rushby [27, 28] formalize assurance cases via defeaters, inductive step confidence, and epistemic probability. In the context of LLM and autonomous agent code generation, recent systems by Chechik et al.—including CLARISSA [29], PLACIDUS [30], and AssureCode [31]—employ assurance cases to monitor agent synthesis, construct safety envelopes, and verify agent-generated artifacts. The refinement-DAG calculus directly complements these frameworks by supplying the underlying software development with a rigorous behavioral foundation: every claim in an assurance case maps directly to a typed behavioral-inclusion proposition (Sat⁡\operatorname{Sat}Sat, Wire⁡\operatorname{Wire}Wire, Dec⁡\operatorname{Dec}Dec, Ref⁡\operatorname{Ref}Ref, Impl⁡\operatorname{Impl}Impl), and the incremental frame theorem provides the exact algebraic conditions under which existing evidential branches remain valid when agent implementations change.

Agent software engineering. Recent work on repository-level coding agents (SWE-bench and related benchmarks) and on self-refinement and reflection shows that agents can iterate on code and tests. The DAG calculus addresses a different point in the loop: it constrains what an agent may accept as a completed step. It is complementary to better code generation, better test generation, and better retrieval; it supplies the missing intermediate behavioral obligations.

11. Limitations and Open Problems

Section titled “11. Limitations and Open Problems”

Connector admissibility. The soundness theorem is only as strong as the connector’s operational soundness and reduction preservation. The theorem is conditional on validity conditions 5 and 6 (executable realization and profile admissibility); those conditions are part of DAG validity, not background assumptions. Rich concurrency — weak memory, Byzantine faults, real-time deadlines — needs richer profiles and correspondingly richer admissibility proofs. The paper’s trace kernel is the base case, not the final word.

Liveness and profiles. The worked example’s safety claim is discharged by the trace kernel; its liveness claim is conditional on the stated fairness and enabling premises and is not derived from the safety proof. A liveness profile needs its own operational composition law and progress-preservation witness, not a relabeling of the safety argument.

Intent correctness. The theorem guarantees that the executable system refines the admitted root intents. It does not guarantee that the root intents are the right requirements. Root authority is an organizational decision; the calculus makes it explicit and auditable, but it cannot make it correct.

Evidence soundness. The gate trusts the evidence checker. A buggy model checker, an inadequate model, or a mis-specified substrate contract can pass a wrong system. The trusted base must be stated and, where possible, minimized. The mechanization target makes the algebraic part small; the operational part remains a hypothesis.

Coverage of context premises. The gate can require explicit context premises for every interface and contract choice, but it cannot force an agent to record every implicit choice inside a leaf implementation. The provenance coverage is the declared obligations and interfaces. A leaf is a trust boundary; its contract is what the parent knows.

Test weakening. The gate blocks weakening of protected intents. It does not prevent an agent from writing a weak test for a property that was never formalized. The remedy is to formalize the property as an intent; the framework makes that remedy visible, not automatic.

Scale. The inspection view of a large DAG can still be large. The calculus bounds the change region by the dependency cone up to proved unchanged boundaries, and it bounds the size of a local proof, but a root-obligation change can reach the whole system, and it does not bound the number of cells or the cost of a single model-checking query. Tool support, proof caching, and model-checking engineering remain necessary.

Empirical validation. The claim that the protocol reduces agent error rates is a hypothesis. The paper’s contribution is the calculus and the gate; a controlled study with arm-independent ground truth is the natural next step.

Decomposition depth and placement of contracts. The DAG topology and the placement of contracts are design decisions. A poor decomposition can make the connector large or the contracts weak. The calculus provides the correctness condition; the architecture remains an engineering choice, guided by the capacity and factoring remarks.

12. Conclusion

Section titled “12. Conclusion”

Software development by agents fails when the gap between a requirement and code is filled by unverified invention. The refinement-DAG calculus closes the gap with explicit intermediate objects: active intents with support, context premises with rationale and reopening conditions, state machines with contracts, and evidence for every behavioral obligation. One relation — behavior inclusion under typed edge abstractions — carries satisfaction, decomposition, edge refinement, and leaf realization. The partial-order acyclicity of the Refinement DAG makes support evaluation an acyclic topological evaluation, makes sibling verification a substitution lemma, enables modular inspection via predecessor/successor closures and root-covering cuts, and makes version evolution reuse every proof at an unchanged interface. The soundness theorem is short because the system is one chain of inclusions, not three bolted-together worlds. The protocol is the operational reading of that chain: read the context, fix the interface, verify the machine, decompose into contracts, substitute the child proof, publish atomically. The durable-acknowledgement example shows the chain catching the exact error that motivates the framework: an agent that treats a volatile write as durable, and a gate that refuses to let it pass.

A.2 Theorem 3 (Incremental Frame and Cutoff), expanded

A.4 Corollary 1 (Pointwise and Frontier Soundness), expanded

Section titled “A.4 Corollary 1 (Pointwise and Frontier Soundness), expanded”

Part 1: Pointwise soundness. For any cell v∈Vv \in Vv∈V, the sub-DAG Desc⁡({v})\operatorname{Desc}(\{v\})Desc({v}) rooted at vvv is a valid finite Refinement DAG satisfying hypotheses (A1)–(A4) of Theorem 1. Instantiating Theorem 1 directly at vvv as root yields Beh⁡exec(v)⊆beh⁡(Mv)\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(v) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_v)Behexec​(v)⊆beh(Mv​). Validity condition 3 yields beh⁡(Mv)⊆⟦c⟧\operatorname{beh}(M_v) \subseteq \llbracket c \rrbracketbeh(Mv​)⊆[[c]] for every active intent c∈A(v)c \in A(v)c∈A(v), whence beh⁡(Mv)⊆Φ(v)=⋂c∈A(v)⟦c⟧\operatorname{beh}(M_v) \subseteq \Phi(v) = \bigcap_{c \in A(v)} \llbracket c \rrbracketbeh(Mv​)⊆Φ(v)=⋂c∈A(v)​[[c]].

Part 2: Frontier soundness. Let C⊆VC \subseteq VC⊆V be a root-covering cut. By definition, CCC is an antichain intersecting every directed path from VrootV_{\mathrm{root}}Vroot​ to VleafV_{\mathrm{leaf}}Vleaf​ at exactly one vertex. Define the upper sub-DAG Anc⁡(C)={ v∈V∣∃u∈C, v→∗u }\operatorname{Anc}(C) = \{\, v \in V \mid \exists u \in C,\ v \to^* u \,\}Anc(C)={v∈V∣∃u∈C, v→∗u}.

No-bypass property. For any internal cell v∈Anc⁡(C)∖Cv \in \operatorname{Anc}(C) \setminus Cv∈Anc(C)∖C, every child c∈ch⁡(v)c \in \operatorname{ch}(v)c∈ch(v) must belong to Anc⁡(C)\operatorname{Anc}(C)Anc(C). For if some c∈ch⁡(v)c \in \operatorname{ch}(v)c∈ch(v) had no path to CCC, then any path from a root r∈Vrootr \in V_{\mathrm{root}}r∈Vroot​ through vvv and ccc to an executable leaf ℓ∈Vleaf\ell \in V_{\mathrm{leaf}}ℓ∈Vleaf​ would bypass CCC entirely, contradicting the assumption that CCC is a root-covering cut. Furthermore, because CCC is an antichain, no vertex in CCC can be a strict descendant of another vertex in CCC.

We prove by well-founded induction on the finite acyclic child relation v→cv \to cv→c on Anc⁡(C)\operatorname{Anc}(C)Anc(C) that for all v∈Anc⁡(C)v \in \operatorname{Anc}(C)v∈Anc(C):

Beh⁡exec(v)  ⊆  HC(v)  ⊆  beh⁡(Mv).\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(v) \;\subseteq\; H_C(v) \;\subseteq\; \operatorname{beh}(M_v).Behexec​(v)⊆HC​(v)⊆beh(Mv​).

Base case (u∈Cu \in Cu∈C). By definition of HCH_CHC​, HC(u)=beh⁡(Mu)H_C(u) = \operatorname{beh}(M_u)HC​(u)=beh(Mu​). The frontier realization hypothesis gives Beh⁡exec(u)⊆beh⁡(Mu)=HC(u)\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(u) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_u) = H_C(u)Behexec​(u)⊆beh(Mu​)=HC​(u). By reflexivity, HC(u)⊆beh⁡(Mu)H_C(u) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_u)HC​(u)⊆beh(Mu​). Both inclusions hold.

Inductive step (v∈Anc⁡(C)∖Cv \in \operatorname{Anc}(C) \setminus Cv∈Anc(C)∖C). Assume the induction hypothesis holds for every child c∈ch⁡(v)c \in \operatorname{ch}(v)c∈ch(v):

Beh⁡exec(c)  ⊆  HC(c)  ⊆  beh⁡(Mc).\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(c) \;\subseteq\; H_C(c) \;\subseteq\; \operatorname{beh}(M_c).Behexec​(c)⊆HC​(c)⊆beh(Mc​).

For unrestricted edges, set Av,c=HXcinA_{v,c} = \mathcal{H}_{X_c}^{\mathrm{in}}Av,c​=HXc​in​.

  1. Lower inclusion (Beh⁡exec(v)⊆HC(v)\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(v) \subseteq H_C(v)Behexec​(v)⊆HC​(v)). Condition 5 (wiring adequacy) and hypothesis (A4) give

By monotonicity of connector KvK_vKv​ (Lemma 1):

By the induction hypothesis, HC(c)⊆beh⁡(Mc)H_C(c) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_c)HC​(c)⊆beh(Mc​) for each ccc, so HC(c) ⁣↾Av,c⊆beh⁡(Mc) ⁣↾Av,cH_C(c)\!\upharpoonright_{A_{v,c}} \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_c)\!\upharpoonright_{A_{v,c}}HC​(c)↾Av,c​​⊆beh(Mc​)↾Av,c​​ and αv,c(HC(c) ⁣↾Av,c)⊆αv,c(beh⁡(Mc) ⁣↾Av,c)\alpha_{v,c}(H_C(c)\!\upharpoonright_{A_{v,c}}) \subseteq \alpha_{v,c}(\operatorname{beh}(M_c)\!\upharpoonright_{A_{v,c}})αv,c​(HC​(c)↾Av,c​​)⊆αv,c​(beh(Mc​)↾Av,c​​). By monotonicity of KvK_vKv​ (Lemma 1):

    HC(v)  =  Kv({αv,c(HC(c) ⁣↾Av,c)}c)  ⊆  Kv({αv,c(beh⁡(Mc) ⁣↾Av,c)}c)  ⊆  Kv({beh⁡(Bv,c)}c).H_C(v) \;=\; K_v\bigl(\{\alpha_{v,c}(H_C(c)\!\upharpoonright_{A_{v,c}})\}_{c}\bigr) \;\subseteq\; K_v\bigl(\{\alpha_{v,c}(\operatorname{beh}(M_c)\!\upharpoonright_{A_{v,c}})\}_{c}\bigr) \;\subseteq\; K_v\bigl(\{\operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c})\}_{c}\bigr).HC​(v)=Kv​({αv,c​(HC​(c)↾Av,c​​)}c​)⊆Kv​({αv,c​(beh(Mc​)↾Av,c​​)}c​)⊆Kv​({beh(Bv,c​)}c​).

    By parent decomposition (Condition 4), Kv({beh⁡(Bv,c)}c)⊆beh⁡(Mv)K_v(\{\operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c})\}_c) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_v)Kv​({beh(Bv,c​)}c​)⊆beh(Mv​). Transitivity yields HC(v)⊆beh⁡(Mv)H_C(v) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_v)HC​(v)⊆beh(Mv​).
